en: Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
A Garland of Verses on the Qualities of the Buddha:
Just as one might weave a beautiful garland from a heap of flowers;
Thus, I have composed more than a thousand verses on the qualities of the Buddha.
To that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One, the Self-Existent, who is perfected in knowledge and conduct—to that Buddha, I pay homage. 1.
Charioteer of those who need to be tamed, knower of the world, unsurpassed;
Teacher of gods and humans—to that Buddha I bow. 2.
Well-gone, well-farer, Lord, giver of happiness, bestower of the state of peace.
I bow down to that Buddha, who has compassion for the entire world. 3.
The Excellent One, the Knower of the Excellent, the Giver of the Excellent, the Supreme Excellent One, the Seizer of the Excellent;
he taught the Excellent Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. 4.
Most auspicious among the auspicious, the auspicious one who is the abode of auspiciousness, the Lord who is the source of auspiciousness—to that Buddha I bow. 5.
The Lord of Auspiciousness, the Auspicious One, the Great Leader of Auspiciousness.
He taught the Dhamma of auspiciousness; I bow down to that Buddha.
6. The leader of the auspicious, the knower of the auspicious, the bestower of the words for the purpose of the auspicious, the one who shows the path of the auspicious—I bow down to that Buddha. 7.
Desiring auspiciousness, longing for auspiciousness, increasing auspiciousness, and perfected by auspicious things—to that Buddha I bow. 8. You illuminate with the light of auspiciousness;
you are the maker of the radiance of the meaning of auspiciousness.
Adorned by the light of auspiciousness, I bow down to that Buddha.
(9) Having attained the goal of auspiciousness, being devoted to the goal of auspiciousness, and always creating auspiciousness—I bow down to that Buddha. (10)
He who sought the path of auspiciousness and attained the supreme auspiciousness;
to that Buddha, the teacher of the way to auspiciousness, I pay homage. 11.
He who upholds the majesty of auspiciousness, the performer of auspiciousness, the Leader;
To him who bestows blessings in every respect, that Buddha, I bow down.
Skilled in what is auspicious and skilled in what is inauspicious,
having attained the supreme blessing— to that Buddha, I bow down.
Endowed with all auspiciousness, sounding the proclamation of auspiciousness,
he taught the supreme auspiciousness— I bow down to that Buddha.
Having sought the meaning of the Great Auspiciousness, the excellent Dharma-auspiciousness was attained.
He proclaimed the path of auspiciousness; I bow down to that Buddha.
(15) He proclaimed the supreme Great Auspiciousness for the sake of householders;
I bow down to that Buddha, the Master and companion of the laity. (16)
Adorned with the great auspiciousness, embellished by the great auspiciousness, the crest-jewel of the great auspiciousness—to that Buddha I bow. 17.
Wearing a garland of the rays of the great auspiciousness, radiant with the attainment of auspiciousness.
He illuminates auspiciousness; I bow down to that Buddha.
(18) A great and precious ocean of auspiciousness, a vast sea of auspiciousness, a mighty ocean of auspiciousness—I bow down to that Buddha. (19)
The ender of the night of inauspiciousness, radiant with the light of the sun of auspiciousness,
scattering the illumination of auspiciousness— I bow down to that Buddha.
(20) Possessed of great learning, the awakener, the one who causes the eye of Dhamma to arise.
I bow down to that Buddha, the ornament of the three worlds.
(21) I bow down to that Buddha, the great speaker, the one who sets [the wheel of Dhamma] in motion, the leader to the goal, the lord, the giver of the Deathless, and the wise one. (22)
By day the sun shines, by night the moon glows;
the Protector shines both by night and by day—to that Buddha I bow.
The warrior shines when he is armored; the brahmin shines when he is meditating.
I bow down to that Buddha, the Protector who practiced austerities without interruption.
24. I bow down to that Buddha, the destroyer of suffering and mental distress, the ender of sorrow and lamentation, who has transcended birth, death, and old age. 25.
One who acts as he speaks, one who speaks as he acts—such is the Tathāgata.
One who acts as he speaks, such is the Buddha; to him I bow down.
He whose passion is destroyed, whose hatred is destroyed, whose delusion is destroyed—he is the Blessed One (Bhagavā).
Having broken pride, having broken conceit—I bow down to that Buddha. 27.
Desiring to break [defilements], with anger broken, with malice broken, with hypocrisy broken;
with taints broken, with craving broken—I bow down to that Buddha. 28.
Broken is birth, broken is death, broken is the world, broken is existence;
broken is saṃsāra, broken is the flood—to that Buddha I bow.
29. Broken of wealth, broken of sorrow, broken of disease, broken of dust;
Broken of the spear, broken of the dart—him, the Buddha, I bow down to.
Broken of hope, broken of envy, broken of craving, with matted locks destroyed;
Broken of desire, broken of bondage—him, the Buddha, I bow down to.
Free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, and free from taints;
free from lust and free from anger—to that Buddha I bow down.
Free from evil, free from merit, free from the burden, and free from stain.
Free from transformation, free from fuel—to that Buddha I bow.
Vomited passion, vomited hatred, vomited delusion, vomited impurity;
vomited taint, vomited thirst—to that Buddha I bow.
Vomited is lust, vomited is hatred, vomited is delusion, vomited is impurity;
vomited is corruption, vomited is craving—to that Buddha I bow. 35.
Teacher of the world, teacher of the three realms, supreme teacher of all beings;
Among leaders, the Great Leader—I bow down to that Buddha.
(36) The Great Teacher, the Teacher of Men, the Teacher of Gods, the Supreme Teacher!
The Eldest Teacher, the Best Teacher—I bow down to that Buddha. (37)
Teacher of all, teacher of the world, teacher of the Dhamma, supreme among teachers;
there is no teacher such as this—him, the Buddha, I pay homage.
38. Great Teacher, great benefactor, great friend, great companion.
I bow down to that Buddha who is a great friend of virtue.
(39) I bow down to that Buddha who possesses great wisdom, great discernment, great learning, and great insight; who is of great intelligence and excellent wisdom. (40)
Greatly pure, greatly auspicious, greatly compassionate, greatly joyful;
greatly divine, greatly capable—I bow down to that Buddha. 41.
Great hero, great steadfast one, great hero, of great strength;
Crushing the great army of Māra, I bow down to that Buddha.
(42) The greatest elder, the most excellent, the one of great splendor, the great leader;
the greatly skillful, the greatly wise—I bow down to that Buddha. (43)
Of great wisdom, of great renown, of great fame, of great glory;
Of great power, of great distinction—to that Buddha I bow.
Greatly contented, greatly joyful, of great speed, of great victory.
Greatly contented and distinguished, I bow down to that Buddha.
45. The great protector, the great master, the great lord, the great sovereign;
the great ruler, the lord of enlightenment, I bow down to that Buddha. 46.
Of great beauty, of great charm, beloved and pleasing to the mind;
of great splendor and delightful—I bow down to that Buddha. 47.
Great meditator, possessor of great wisdom, of great intelligence and great purity;
Possessing great power and wisdom, I bow down to that Buddha.
(48) Greatly patient and enduring, free from great doubt, a guardian of the Dhamma;
greatly restrained and self-controlled, I bow down to that Buddha. (49)
Greatly honored, worshipped, highly esteemed, and saluted;
Even more greatly revered—I bow down to that Buddha.
Of great purpose, seeking the great, possessing the great goal, and most exalted.
Great, having attained greatness—I bow down to that Buddha.
A great recipient of gain, a great doer, a great giver, a great possessor of wealth;
a great possessor of knowledge, a great object of veneration—I bow down to that Buddha.
Of great intelligence, O Great Wise One, the preeminent hero of great awakening;
having crossed the great ocean of existence, I bow down to that Buddha. 53.
A great Naga, of great fortune, great-armed and of great psychic power.
The great warrior, the sublime one—I bow down to that Buddha. (54) The one with great teeth, the greatly peaceful one, the great teacher, the one of great virtues;
the giver of the state of supreme peace—I bow down to that Buddha. (55)
Of great virtue, of great mind, the great awakened one, the great seer;
having crossed the great ocean of delusion—to that Buddha I bow.
56. Of great asceticism, seeking the Dhamma, of great fame, the Leader.
Greatly glorious and full of splendor, I bow down to that Buddha.
(57) Of great radiance and great light, the shatterer of the darkness of delusion;
he lit the lamp of wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha. (58)
The giver of great tranquility, the King of Sages, the Lord of Sages;
the giver of peace, the giver of happiness—to that Buddha I bow. 59.
He who has transcended the great hindrances, having utterly destroyed great delusion;
I bow down to that Buddha who has crossed over the great flood and attained liberation.
(60) I bow down to that Buddha who has abandoned the great substrate of existence, who destroyed greed and hatred, and who crushed the great enemy. (61)
Having attained the power of the great higher knowledges, the destroyer of great conceit, he demonstrated the Great True Dhamma—to that Buddha, I pay homage. 62.
Always pure day and night, the supreme leader of the great world.
Renowned throughout the entire world, I bow down to that Buddha.
(63) Having severed great ignorance, having cast off the great snare of attachment, you have untangled the great tangle; I bow down to that Buddha. (64)
I bow down to that Buddha, who has removed the great dart, dispelled the great thorn, and brought an end to the great taints.
He is one of great prowess, a hero, and utterly unconquered in every way. 65.
The Hero who possesses absolute fearlessness— to that Buddha I bow.
He who has transcended great craving, who has dispelled great sorrow,
and who has overcome great suffering— to that Buddha I bow.
I bow to that Buddha who has transcended great conceit,
who crushed the army of Māra, and who exhausted the defilements of karma.
He has crossed the great ocean of existence and reached the further shore beyond all evil.
I bow down to that Buddha who has transcended the great cycle of existence. 69.
I bow down to that Buddha who has passed beyond the great fetters, who is the destroyer of the great whirlpool, and who has crossed over the great flood of saṃsāra. 70.
I bow down to that Buddha who cleanses great passion, who crushes great hatred, and who dried up the great flood. He who dwells in great loving-kindness,
who possesses great merit, and who is most sublime.
To that Buddha, an ocean of great compassion, I bow down. 72.
Having crossed the great ocean of existence, liberated from existence, having reached the end of existence, with the thorn of sorrow utterly severed—to that Buddha, I bow down. 73.
Having transcended the path of the great forest, having reached the further shore of the great wilderness, having crossed over the flood of the great mass of existence—to that Buddha I bow. 74.
Having attained the fruit of the Great Path, well-arrived at the ocean of the Deathless;
I bow to that Buddha who analyzed the wheel of existence (bhavacakka). 75.
I bow to that Buddha who, endowed with great and perfect enlightenment and well-cultivated in the path to liberation, shattered the bonds of existence (bhavabandhana). 76.
I bow down to that Buddha who has utterly eradicated great delight,
who has emerged from the great defilements, and who has crossed over the flood of great evil.
He has completely exhausted great craving and has cast off the great fetters.
He has dispelled all taints—I bow down to that Buddha. 78.
He shattered the darkness of delusion like the sun, the maker of light;
he radiated great splendor—I bow down to that Buddha. 79.
He has shattered great fear, he who, with trembling severed, is the dispeller of fear;
the Buddha who destroys the great mass of suffering—to him I bow. 80.
He destroyed the great enemy, the wielder of the sword, possessed of great power.
The great accomplished one, the one of great authority—to that Buddha I bow. 81.
He who dispelled the great darkness and was the illuminator of the great light;
he who shone like the sun—to that Buddha I bow. 82.
I bow down to that Buddha who has renounced great wealth, who has crossed the great ocean of the three cravings, and who has gone beyond the sea of delusion.
He has attained the power of the great higher knowledges; he is the leader through the great exertion.
Liberated from the great fetters, to that Buddha I bow. 84.
A great ocean of supreme enlightenment, a sea of great perfect awakening;
a vast reservoir of great wisdom, to that Buddha I bow. 85.
The Great Physician, Lord of Ascetics, the healer of the disease of craving;
you liberated many from suffering—I bow down to that Buddha.
86. Adorned with great majesty, the wielder of six-colored rays of light;
Pervasive with great radiance, I bow down to that Buddha. 87.
Attained to great compassion, always delighting in loving-kindness, rejoicing in the welfare of the great multitude, I bow down to that Buddha. 88.
I bow down to that Buddha who destroyed great wrong view, who proclaimed the Great True Dhamma, who severed the great continuity of the cycle of existence,
and who extracted the thorn of great sorrow. He is the purifier of the great stake.
He who brings great peace to the world—to that Buddha I bow.
(90) He who has washed away the mire of great evil, the liberator from great suffering, he who purified the great virtuous ones—to that Buddha I bow. (91)

He crushed pride and deceit; I bow down to that Buddha.
(93) He destroyed great delusion, he was the one who brought about the cessation of great passion, and he extinguished great hatred; I bow down to that Buddha. (94)
To the one who speaks diverse Dhamma, the proclaimer of the marvelous path, the great teacher, the great orator—to that Buddha, I pay homage. 95.
To the great speaker, the proponent of karma, the supreme Sage of the Śākyas.
The bull among sages, the lord of sages—to that Buddha I bow.
96. Seated upon the night of great delusion, possessing great radiance and expansive;
illuminating with the great moonlight—to that Buddha I bow. 97.
I bow down to that Buddha who destroyed the night of great ignorance,
who is adorned with the radiance of true knowledge, and who causes the light of the Great Dhamma to shine forth.
He crushed great delusion and is the liberator from the net of illusion.
You crushed false doctrine; I bow down to that Buddha. 99.
You dried up the stream of the taints, you who have subdued great ill-will;
having crossed the great ocean of delusion, I bow down to that Buddha. 100.
Having transcended great delusion, having dispelled great fear, and having crossed over the great flood of existence—to that Buddha I bow. 101.
He is abstinent from taking life, one who has laid aside the rod, and is non-violent.
To that ocean of immeasurable loving-kindness, to that Buddha, I bow down. 102.
Abstaining from taking what is not given, free from desire, without possessions, a giver of all, one who has transcended passion—to that Buddha, I bow down. 103.
Having transcended unchaste conduct and renounced the enjoyment of sensual pleasures, you crushed the pride of Māra’s daughters—I bow down to that Buddha. 104.
You are a protector of the body, well-tamed; a protector of speech, firm in your vows.
Endowed with great virtue, I bow down to that Buddha. 105.
Endowed with right livelihood, walking in pure conduct, the Lord who is the crest-jewel of morality—I bow down to that Buddha. 106.
Easy to support, perfected in virtue, the crest-jewel of pure conduct;
steadfast and endowed with speed—to that Buddha I bow. 107.
Without conceptualization, without applied thought, without sustained thought, and beyond the reach of the mind;
Having attained one-pointedness of mind, I bow down to that Buddha.
(108) He well guarded his sense faculties, mindful and with a restrained mind;
with a perfectly concentrated heart, I bow down to that Buddha. (109)
Possessing abundant wisdom, knowing wisdom, resplendent with profound wisdom, endowed with perfect wisdom, the eye of wisdom—to that Buddha I bow. 110.
Abounding in wisdom, truly wise, possessed of broad wisdom, the wise one.
Skilled in knowledge, the eye of wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha.
(111) Sharp in wisdom, swift in wisdom, full of wisdom, the source of wisdom;
the lord of wisdom, the master of wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha. (112)
To him of constant wisdom, of established wisdom, of firm wisdom, the giver of wisdom;
to him of purified wisdom—that Buddha, I pay homage. 113.
To him who has reached perfection in wisdom, the pinnacle of infinite wisdom;
Endowed with the perfection of merit, I bow down to that Buddha.
(114) Rich in wisdom, powerful in wisdom, established in the virtue of wisdom;
Lord of wisdom, bearer of wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha. (115)
Possessing wisdom, possessing a refined intellect, with steady wisdom and a treasury of wisdom;
an ocean of wisdom, one who has mastered wisdom—to that Buddha I bow. 116.
Skilled in the proficiency of wisdom, possessing infinite wisdom, the All-pervading One.
Possessing supreme wisdom, possessing foremost wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha.
(117) Possessing perfect wisdom, full, the one who has reached the further shore of excellent wisdom;
Lord of wisdom, Lord of knowledge—I bow down to that Buddha. (118)
To him of ultimate stainless wisdom, possessed of perfect eloquence, the bearer of the wisdom of penetration—to that Buddha, I bow. 119.
To the one of peerless wisdom, the peerless, the one of vast wisdom, the supreme among the wise.
Pure in wisdom and purified—O Buddha, I bow down to you. 120.
The Protector with penetrating wisdom, with awakening wisdom, and skillful;
pure in wisdom and thoroughly cleansed—O Buddha, I bow down to you. 121.
The eye of wisdom, the eye of knowledge, the Buddha-eye, possessed of the excellent eye;
the all-seeing one, perfectly complete—to that Buddha I bow.
Endowed with powerful wisdom, sharp intelligence, and consisting of discernment.
Possessing full direct knowledge, he is the Knower of All; I bow down to that Buddha.
(123) Endowed with the weapon of wisdom, invincible, unconquered, and powerful;
the Victor has conquered the Evil One; I bow down to that Buddha. (124)
Having attained the unconditioned, adorned with the ornament of wisdom, he proclaimed the ultimate truth; I bow down to that Buddha. 125.
Wise, he extended his wisdom; knowing, he increased his knowledge.
The destroyer of non-Dhamma, the possessor of Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
126. Crowned with wisdom, lord of wisdom; lord of knowledge, crowned with knowledge;
crowned with Dhamma, lord of Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. 127.
Possessing swift wisdom, self-conquered, liberated from all fetters;
released from bonds and guarding the sense-doors—to that Buddha I bow. 128.
Possessed of great wisdom, performing much service, possessing vast knowledge and manifold virtues;
Endowed with manifold virtues, I bow down to that Buddha.
(129) Endowed with wisdom and liberation, having transcended delusion and gone beyond suffering, the one who has extracted the thorn of the defilements—I bow down to that Buddha. (130)
The Perfectly Awakened One whose heart is enlightenment, whose lord is wisdom and whose mind is wisdom;
whose consciousness is knowledge and whose radiance is knowledge—to that Buddha I bow down. 131.
He whose virtue is constant, whose mind is constant, whose resolve is constant, and whose conduct is constant;
Firmly liberated, firmly attained—I bow down to that Buddha.
(132) Strong in virtue, strong in mind, strong in wisdom, strong in final knowledge;
strong in the Dharma, strong in steadfastness—I bow down to that Buddha. (133)
Rich in virtue, rich in mind, rich in wisdom, rich in higher knowledge;
rich in the Dhamma, rich in steadfastness—to that Buddha I bow down. 134.
He is restrained by bodily restraint, restrained by verbal restraint;
Restrained by the restraint of mind, I bow down to that Buddha.
(135) Having reached the pinnacle of virtue, attained concentration, and perfected wisdom through thorough cultivation;
drinking the nectar-essence of the Dhamma, I bow down to that Buddha. (136)
Virtuous, having attained concentration, adorned with the ornament of wisdom,
and graced by the jewelry of the Dhamma— to that Buddha I bow.
Adorned with right concentration and beautified by virtue and wisdom.
Having attained the power of all direct knowledges, I bow down to that Buddha.
(138) Pure in virtue, pure in mind, pure in wisdom, and pure in thought, he proclaimed the pure Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha. (139)
Virtuous, well-concentrated, wise, and renowned, a seer celebrated throughout the world and well-known—I bow down to that Buddha. 140.
Endowed with virtue and concentration, steadfast, and preeminent in wisdom;
He awakened everyone to everything; I bow down to that Buddha.
(141) Possessor of infinite knowledge, one who contemplates, the crest-jewel upon the head of wisdom;
the eye of wisdom, the preeminent among men—I bow down to that Buddha. (142)
The supreme leader of leaders, the Protector, possessed of knowledge, filled with knowledge;
capable in knowledge, established in knowledge—to that Buddha I bow. 143.
Delighting in knowledge, rejoicing in knowledge, skilled in profound knowledge.
Endowed with knowledge and vision, to that Buddha I bow.
Adorned by wisdom, a peak of wisdom, decorated with the ornament of wisdom;
the crest-jewel of wisdom, the wise one—to that Buddha I bow.
Possessor of knowledge, supreme in knowledge, mountain of knowledge, possessing empty knowledge;
ocean of knowledge, sea of knowledge—to that Buddha I bow. 146.
Crown of knowledge, seal of knowledge, lamp of knowledge, crest of knowledge;
O mountain of knowledge, O horn of wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha.
(147) Profound in knowledge, wise, sharp in insight, and far-sighted—you who shattered the root of ignorance—I bow down to that Buddha. (148)
The All-Knowing One, known as the Omniscient, the Teacher who sets things right, has expounded the pure Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha. 149.
He who has attained the knowledge of omniscience, the All-Wise Guide.
Having attained the bliss of Nibbāna, I bow down to that Buddha.
(150) All-knowing, possessed of all-knowledge, having abandoned all conceiving on every side, with all fermentations exhausted— I bow down to that Buddha. (151)
Lord of all-knowing, capable, supreme, and powerful;
seeing with knowledge and vision in every respect—to that Buddha I bow. 152.
The Naga who is the lord of the ten powers, the sovereign of immeasurable knowledge.
Having attained great supernormal power, I bow down to that Buddha.
153. Endowed with the knowledge of penetration, the cutter of the veil of illusion, he utterly consumed ignorance; I bow down to that Buddha. 154.
I bow to that Buddha who sought the knowledge of liberation, who proclaimed the truth of the path, who is the teacher of the path and the knower of the path.
He destroyed all ignorance, he who is supreme among those of great wisdom. 155.
I bow down to that Buddha, the great ocean of the knowledge of enlightenment.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained right vision,
who is established in right knowledge, and whose self is conquered through right liberation.
The Arahant, perfected in true knowledge, crowned with the pinnacle of wisdom, who has attained supreme bliss—to that Buddha I bow. 158.
Perfected in supreme knowledge, filled with excellent discernment;
Having attained right liberation, I bow down to that Buddha. 159.
All-seeing, empty-minded, wise in all duties, endowed everywhere with excellent qualities—I bow down to that Buddha. 160.
Having fully experienced all sensations, he awakened to perfect enlightenment;
free from sorrow, of noble mind—to that Buddha I bow. 161.
Free from craving for sensations, liberated from sensations in every way;
To him who has mastered the Vedas and reached their end—to that Buddha, I bow.
(162) The ground of trust for all beings, like eyes to the blind;
the protector who needs no protection—to that Buddha, I bow. (163)
Witness of suffering, one who has exhausted suffering, knower of suffering, one who has reached the end of suffering;
one who has abandoned suffering, knower of suffering—to that Buddha I bow. 164.
Witness of the body, witness of the mind, happy witness of feelings;
A witness to the Dhamma, a true witness—I bow down to that Buddha.
(165) With body tranquil, speech tranquil, mind tranquil, and composed;
with all substrata of existence stilled—I bow down to that Buddha. (166)
With mind perfectly concentrated, established in right virtue, and perfected in right wisdom—to that Buddha I bow. 167.
One who has attained the ultimate goal of all things, yet whose insight is excessively over-exerted;
Having attained complete peace, I bow down to that Buddha.
(168) Having fully experienced the entire body and having insight into all phenomena, you abandoned the cycle of existence; I bow down to that Buddha. (169)
Always endowed with mindfulness, always delighting in clear comprehension, the peaceful master of ascetics—to that Buddha I bow. 170.
Seeing the vision of truth, possessing insight into the true Dhamma;
He set in motion the Wheel of Truth; I bow down to that Buddha.
171. Perfect in the subtlety of meditative absorption, having reached the further shore of his own aspirations, seeing the peril in existence; I bow down to that Buddha. 172.
To the one possessed of vision, possessed of vows, possessed of virtue, and perfectly virtuous;
to the one possessed of wisdom, possessed of insight—to that Buddha I bow. 173.
To the one possessed of beauty, possessed of qualities, possessed of radiance, and the bearer of light.
To him who is possessed of glory and renown, that Buddha, I pay homage.
To him who is possessed of mindfulness, self-restraint, peace, wisdom, and intelligence;
to him who is possessed of splendor and sagacity—that Buddha, I pay homage.
Possessing yoga, possessing security, possessing eloquence, and being powerful;
possessing moral shame, possessing glory—to that Buddha I bow. 176.
Self-controlled, free from pride, wise, steadfast, and bearing the burden.
Endowed with fortitude and perfected in wisdom, I bow down to that Buddha.
(177) Possessed of strength, possessed of supernormal power, compassionate and the abode of mercy;
radiant and beautiful in form, I bow down to that Buddha. (178)
Endowed with patience, endowed with peace, Blessed Ones, perfectly complete;
Possessing the method, possessing the guide, that Buddha I bow down to.
Endowed with enlightenment, endowed with wisdom, the knowledge of enlightenment, the quality of enlightenment.
Having attained the true Dhamma, I bow down to that Buddha. 180.
Free from faults, possessed of loving-kindness, possessed of compassion, rejoicing, and in every way possessed of equanimity—I bow down to that Buddha. 181.
To those who are self-restrained and walk with restraint, who are patient and happy, who possess austerity and suchness—to that Buddha I bow down. 182.
To the person who possesses power, who is majestic and eloquent;
I bow down to that Buddha who illuminates the true goal.
I bow down to that Buddha whose fetters are severed, whose attachments are severed, whose passion is severed, whose delight is severed, whose craving is severed. 184.
With doubts severed, with anxiety severed, with uncertainty severed, with defilement severed;
with all fetters severed—to that Buddha I bow down. 185.
With attachment severed, with clinging severed, with grasping severed, with turbidity severed;
With bonds severed and supports cut away, I bow down to that Buddha.
(186) With desire severed, with anger severed, with resentment severed, and with pride severed;
with defilements severed and agitation severed—I bow down to that Buddha. (187)
With evil cut off, with torment cut off, with craving cut off, with doubt cut off;
with the stream cut off, with attachment cut off—to that Buddha I bow down.
With worldly enjoyment cut off, with fetters cut off, with fear cut off, with terror cut off.
With severed trunk and severed will, I bow down to that Buddha.
(189) With shattered fear, shattered affliction, shattered doubt, and shattered craving;
with shattered delight and shattered hunger, I bow down to that Buddha. (190)
I bow to that Buddha who has shattered agitation, shattered suffering, shattered defilements, and shattered the thicket of doubt;
who has shattered conceit, shattered passion, shattered greed, shattered fickleness, shattered anger, and shattered strife.
191. He who has shattered lust, shattered longing, shattered wrath, and shattered conflict.
I bow down to that Buddha who has transcended conceit, who has transcended weariness. 192.

I bow down to that Buddha who has transcended worldly enjoyment, who has transcended sorrow, who has transcended disease, who has destroyed the dust [of passion], who has pierced through the stake, and who has removed the arrow. 193.
He who has shattered the assembly, shattered the stage, shattered passion, and shattered delight;
who has shattered joy and shattered craving—to that Buddha I bow.
He who has shattered all the ailments of existence and shattered the great darkness of delusion.
Distinct from worldly conditions, distinct from diseases—I bow to that Buddha.
195. Free from weariness, free from greed, free from delusion, free from longing, free from desire;
free from avarice, free from covetousness—I bow to that Buddha. 196.
Wearied by hope, wearied by envy, wearied by craving, and wearied like a hunted deer;
wearied by desire and wearied by bondage—to that Buddha I bow. 197.
Wearied by the eon, wearied by time, and wearied by the defilements in every way.
Root-destroyed, thorn-destroyed—to that Buddha I bow down.
(198) Crossed over evil, crossed over merit, crossed over delusion, crossed over impurity;
crossed over change, crossed over craving—to that Buddha I bow down. (199)
Crossed over fault, crossed over hatred, crossed over passion, crossed over possessiveness;
crossed over burning, crossed over despair—I bow down to that Buddha.
Crossed over birth, crossed over death, crossed over the world, crossed over existence.
One who has crossed the flood, one who has crossed saṃsāra—I bow down to that Buddha.
(201) One whose delusion is crushed, whose pride is crushed, whose conceit is crushed, whose intoxication is crushed;
one whose passion is crushed, whose hatred is crushed—I bow down to that Buddha. (202)
I bow down to that Buddha who is the powdering of anger, the powdering of malice, the powdering of agitation, and the powdering of fear; the powdering of the spear, the powdering of the dart.
He is the powdering of evil, the powdering of merit, the powdering of self, and the powdering of possessiveness.
You are the powder that grinds away doubt, the powder that grinds away suspicion; I bow down to that Buddha. 204.
You have ground the wheel of saṃsāra to dust;
you are the one who has snapped the rope of existence; you have pulverized all conditioned phenomena; I bow down to that Buddha. 205.
Without possessiveness, without egoism, without support, without abode;
free from conceptual proliferation, without undertaking—that Buddha I bow down to.
206. Without attachment, without expectation, without doubt, without anxiety;
Taintless and free from longing, to that Buddha I bow. 207.
Fearless, free from affliction, free from desire, and free from defilement;
unstained and beyond doubt, to that Buddha I bow. 208.
Washed, cleansed, and purified, extinguished and one who has crossed over;
stainless and having attained cessation—to that Buddha I bow. 209.
Fearless, the bull among men, unshakable, the lion among men.
Narakuñjara, free from trepidation—I bow down to that Buddha. 210.
Free from passion and free from anger, free from impurity and free from pride;
free from suffering and free from sorrow—I bow down to that Buddha. 211.
The destroyer of various sectarian views, the shatterer of diverse doctrines, who warded off manifold wrong beliefs—to that Buddha I bow. 212.
He whose craving has ended, who has attained Nibbāna, who is free from desire and without fuel.
Free from attachment, free from craving—I bow down to that Buddha. 213.
Unbound, yet bound [to the world of beings], free from affliction, free from corruption;
without bolt, without thorn—I bow down to that Buddha. 214.
Free from affliction, free from evil, free from thirst, and undisturbed;
free from agitation, free from movement—that Buddha I revere. 215. One who has subdued pride, who is without guile, and who possesses the knowledge of the certainty of the path.
Having crossed over doubt and being free from fear, I bow down to that Buddha.
216. Free from arrogance, free from resentment, without conceit, and undisturbed;
having attained Nibbāna and being entirely pure, I bow down to that Buddha. 217.
Free from aversion and without hatred, without anger and without malice;
having attained the fixed course of rightness and being joyful—I bow down to that Buddha.
218. Most skillful, having found the method, stainless and having reached Nirvana;
I bow down to that Buddha who has transcended death and the realm of Namuci.
219. Free from greed, free from affection, free from exertion, free from desire, free from conceit, and free from attachment—I bow down to that Buddha. 220.
Free from pride, free from craving, the destroyer of delight and lust;
free from desire, unattached—to that Buddha I bow. 221.
Free from hatred, free from hypocrisy, the uprooter of the craving that leads to existence.
Free from impurity, free from malice—I bow down to that Buddha. 222.
Free from defilement, unshakable, immovable, eternally steady;
ever-guarded and free from agitation—I bow down to that Buddha. 223.
Free from guile and free from crookedness, without hypocrisy and without deceit;
free from bonds and without fault—to that Buddha I bow.
Free from hypocrisy, with pride subdued, and without longing for existence or non-existence.
Free from doubt and devoid of craving, I bow down to that Buddha. 225.
Destroyer of Namuci’s army, ascetic who delights in the signless, subtle and having crossed the flood—I bow down to that Buddha. 226.
Free from harshness and free from thorns, free from resentment and delighting in Nibbāna;
free from negligence and free from bondage—to that Buddha I bow. 227.
Free from conceit and free from pride, free from craving and free from deceit;
Free from doubt and devoid of desire, I bow down to that Buddha. 228.
A hero among men, steadfast among men, the knower of men, the best of men;
a man-elephant, a lion among men—I bow down to that Buddha. 229.
Foremost among men, best of men, bull among men, supreme among men;
the excellent charioteer who tames men—to that Buddha I bow. 230.
Supreme lord, lord of men, lord of the world, conqueror of the world.
The Lord of Devas, the Lord of Brahmas—to that Buddha I bow. 231.
Delighting in meditation, a contemplative who has destroyed the poison of the defilements, perfected in subtle jhāna—to that Buddha I bow. 232.
The Protector whose mind is free from craving, whose mind is ever stainless,
whose mind is untainted and who is generous— to that Buddha I bow down. (233) One who has cast off birth,
cast off death, cast off the world, and cast off existence.
Pushed back is his worldly existence, pushed back is the flood; I bow down to that Buddha.
(234) Pushed back is hesitation, pushed back is anxiety, pushed back is hunger, and pushed back is longing;
pushed back is delight in the world, pushed back is craving; I bow down to that Buddha. (235)
He who has dispelled remorse, dispelled evil, dispelled burning, and dispelled the taints;
he who has dispelled conceit and overweening pride—to that Buddha I bow. 236.
He who dispels greed, dispels longing, dispels anger, and dispels intoxication.
The dispeller of directions, the dispeller of views—I bow to that Buddha.
The dispeller of karma, the dispeller of defilements, the dispeller of strife, from whom impurity has been shaken away;
the dispeller of ignorance in every way—I bow to that Buddha.
I bow down to that Buddha who dispels all the afflictions of existence,
who has driven away the great darkness of delusion, and who removes mental anguish and physical disease.
(239) He whose wisdom is swift and whose wisdom is ever-fresh, who is compassionate and whose compassion is ever-flowing.
O ocean of wisdom, ocean of loving-kindness—I bow down to that Buddha.
O treasure-store of knowledge, ocean of knowledge; treasure-store of Dhamma, ocean of Dhamma;
treasure-store of virtues, ocean of virtues—I bow down to that Buddha.
Free from attachment, free from fear, free from longing, free from dwelling;
free from hope, free from clinging—to that Buddha I bow down.
Free from craving, free from stain, free from timidity, free from dread.
Free from stinginess, free from grasping—I bow down to that Buddha. 243.
Free from desire, free from craving, free from passion, free from longing;
free from will, free from delight—I bow down to that Buddha. 244.
I bow down to that Buddha who is greedy for liberation, covetous of liberation, longing for liberation, seeking liberation, desirous of liberation, and yearning for liberation—
like a bird freed from a net, who is liberated from existence after existence. 245.
Liberated from the fetters, to that Buddha I bow.
(246) Liberated in mind, possessed of jhāna; liberated by wisdom, possessed of wisdom;
doubly liberated—to that Buddha I bow. (247)
Liberated from all sense-bases, the Lord of Sages has attained final Nibbāna;
freed from the cycle of birth, I bow down to that Buddha. 248.
Liberated from all defilements, fallen away from all mental distress;
Free from all seeking, to that Buddha I bow.
(249) Free from the seeking of sensual pleasures, liberated also from the seeking of existence, and released from the seeking of non-existence—to that Buddha I bow. (250)
I bow to that Buddha who is liberated from the state of desiring,
freed from the state of becoming, and released from the state of non-becoming.
He is liberated from the craving for sensual pleasures and is the shatterer of the craving for existence.
To him whose craving for existence has been exhausted— to that Buddha, I bow down.
Freed from the disease of all sensual desires, the physician for the disease of existence,
liberated from the disease of passion— to that Buddha, I bow down.
Freed from suffering, attained to happiness, liberated from self, having realized non-self;
freed from the impermanent, knowing the permanent—I bow down to that Buddha.
254. Freed from anger, freed from wrath, freed from defilements, freed from hypocrisy;
Freed from passion, freed from deceit—I bow down to that Buddha.
Freed from illusion, freed from delusion, freed from pride, freed from intoxication;
freed from conceit, freed from infatuation—I bow down to that Buddha.
Freed from hatred, freed from ill-will, freed from worldly attachment, like one who has attained liberation;
freed from views, freed from evil—him I bow to as the Buddha.
257. Freed from greed, freed from longing, freed from anger, a deliverer.
Freed from craving, freed from weariness—I bow down to that Buddha.
(258) Freed from worldly enjoyment, freed from sorrow, freed from disease, with dust removed;
freed from the stake, freed from the dart—I bow down to that Buddha. (259)
Freed from attachment, freed from passion, freed from lust, he delights in liberation;
freed from delight, freed from craving—to that Buddha I bow.
Freed from agitation, freed from fuel, freed from desire, he is one whose protection is liberation.
Free from hunger, free from thirst, I bow down to that Buddha.
(261) Free from calamity, free from fear, free from trepidation, one whose fears are released;
free from mental distress, free from disease, I bow down to that Buddha. (262)
Freed from the womb, freed from deceit, freed from fraud, freed from fear;
freed from burning, freed from fever—him, the Buddha, I pay homage.
Freed from desire, freed from duty, freed from wavering, freed from delusion.
Freed from the cycle of existence, freed from the flood—O Buddha, I bow down to you.
Freed from birth, freed from death, freed from the world, with existence liberated;
freed from craving, freed from the fetter—I bow down to that Buddha.
Freed from hope, freed from envy, freed from craving, the one who has attained liberation;
freed from the forest of defilements, freed from longing—I bow down to that Buddha.
Freed from the ear, freed from the yoke, freed from contact, he whose very essence is liberation.
Freed from the root, freed from the burden—to that Buddha I bow. 267.
Freed from this shore, freed from the further shore, freed from the terrible, freed from grasping;
freed from the eon, freed from time—to that Buddha I bow. 268.
Freed from evil, freed from merit, freed from "I," and free from the conceit of "mine";
freed from doubt, freed from suspicion—to that Buddha I bow down.
Freed from sloth, freed from torpor, freed from fever, and free from thirst.
Free from heat, free from distress—I bow down to that Buddha.
(270) Freed from the aggregates, freed from bondage, freed from strife, with taints released;
entirely freed from thirst—I bow down to that Buddha. (271)
Free from sustained thought and initial application, always perfectly concentrated,
with a mind rightly directed— to that Buddha I bow.
Free from a mind struck by affliction, and free from all fears;
Freed from fear, freed from terror—to that Buddha I bow.
(273) Having established the conventional designation while seeing the ultimate truth, and being completely free from distortions—to that Buddha I bow. (274)
Liberated through the cultivation of the mind, freed from all sufferings, and released from all calamities—to that Buddha I bow down. 275.
Liberated from a distracted mind, his heart is always steadfast.
Liberated from a mind of conflict, I bow down to that Buddha.
(276) Liberated from a mind of malice, with a mind always cultivated, and free from a heedless mind, I bow down to that Buddha. (277)
Liberated from the mind of acquisitions, always with a mind intent on deliverance,
liberated from a mind of longing— to that Buddha I bow. Liberated from a mind of expectation,
always with a mind free from attachment.
Liberated by the mind through exertion, I bow down to that Buddha.
(279) Perfectly liberated, the Fully Awakened One, the Sage whose mind is well-liberated, freed through perfect knowledge—I bow down to that Buddha. (280)
I bow down to that Buddha whose mind is undefiled, who is liberated from all states of existence, and who is intent upon transcending all dogmatic attachments.
He is freed from the darkness of the three worlds and illuminates them with the radiance of his wisdom.
Having crossed over the craving for existence, I bow down to that Buddha.
Freed from negligence, skilled, with a mind delighting in meditation,
liberated from the ocean of existence— I bow down to that Buddha.
Freed from the formations of saṃsāra, with a mind free from change, liberated from the ninefold mass [of defilements]—I bow down to that Buddha. 284.
Freed from birth, sickness, and old age, the Conqueror of Māra is himself free from death.
Freed from renewed existence, to that Buddha I bow. 285.
Freed from impurity and purified, with a mind eternally stainless;
pure with a well-cultivated heart, to that Buddha I bow. 286.
Freed from the darkness of ignorance, illuminating the light of true knowledge, knowing all things with complete wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha. 287.
Freed from attachment, unstained, his mind released from attachment to objects.
Free from delusion and pride, I bow down to that Buddha.
(288) Liberated from worldly existence and its enjoyments, the cutter of the fetters of becoming, who has transcended the fear of the terror of existence—I bow down to that Buddha. (289)
Freed from hatred and anger, he dried up the venom of malice;
he crushed the dart of sorrow—I bow down to that Buddha. 290.
Free from the seed [of rebirth], endowed with power, having well-awakened, he is possessed of sublime wisdom.
Freed from greed and endowed with wisdom, I bow down to that Buddha.
(291) Freed from the affliction of all existence, freed from the great darkness of delusion, and liberated from childishness and deceit, I bow down to that Buddha. (292)
Liberated from the "that," liberated from the "this," liberated from agitation in every way;
liberated from all thirsting—him I bow to, that Buddha. 293.
Liberated from the conduit to existence, his mind released from the flood of existence.
In every respect liberated from bondage—to that Buddha I bow.
(294) Liberated from the yoke of all desires, extinguished by the fire of all desires, liberated from delight in all desires—to that Buddha I bow. (295)
Freed from all matted locks, liberated from all attachment, freed from all underlying tendencies—to that Buddha I bow. 296.
Completely released from all taints, with a mind forever undaunted;
Completely liberated from all attachments, I bow down to that Buddha.
(297) Freed from all dangers, a lion with a fearless mind, in every way released from bondage, I bow down to that Buddha. (298)
Freed from all doubt, with a mind undisturbed by influxes, liberated from suffering in every state—I bow down to that Buddha. 299.
Liberated from all objects of perception, the destroyer of existence in every way.
With all underlying tendencies severed, I bow down to that Buddha.
(300) Completely liberated from all longing, with a mind forever unstained and freed from all covetousness, I bow down to that Buddha. (301)
Free from the fuel of mental agitation, free from delusion and intoxication, and liberated from all greed—to that Buddha I bow. 302.
Free from all abuse, with a mind full of loving-kindness;
Freed from the crookedness of cupidity, I bow down to that Buddha.
(303) Freed from all contraction, freed from ill-will at all times, freed from resistance in every respect—I bow down to that Buddha. (304)
Liberated from all desires, freed from longing in every way, liberated from all craving—to that Buddha I bow. 305.
Freed from both opposition and compliance, forever free from agitation;
Completely liberated from all remorse, I bow down to that Buddha.
(306) Always free from confusion, entirely free from delusion, and everywhere free from ignorance—I bow down to that Buddha. (307)
Liberated from wandering in every place, liberated from wandering in all respects;
liberated from all perversions—to that Buddha I bow. 308.
Liberated from the bitter and the astringent, liberated from harshness in every way.
Always free from impurity, I bow down to that Buddha. 309.
Liberated from devouring everything, always free from social entanglement, and released from aggression, I bow down to that Buddha. 310.
The sage who is released from the notion of "I," liberated from the notion of "mine," and freed from honor and dishonor—to that Buddha I bow. 311.
He who is released from all fetters and forever freed from the obstacle;
I bow down to that Buddha, the conqueror of all, liberated from all. 312.
I bow down to that Buddha, completely released from all exertion, forever free from conceptual proliferation (*papañca*), and liberated from all acquisitions (*upadhi*). 313.
Freed from the extreme of hypocrisy, freed from crookedness in every way;
Freed from all ill-will, to that Buddha I bow.
Freed from dejection, with a mind freed from greed;
Completely liberated from all fevers, I bow down to that Buddha.
(315) Liberated from all conceits, released from all fevers, and freed from agitation in every respect, I bow down to that Buddha. (316)
Freed from all hindrances, perfected, with a one-pointed mind;
possessed of right wisdom, rightly liberated—to that Buddha I bow down. 317.
Freed from all turbidity, pure, with a thoroughly purified heart;
Freed from the stain of harshness, I bow down to that Buddha. 318.
Freed from all ill-will, with a mind always serene, and liberated from all resentment, I bow down to that Buddha. 319.
Freed from all negligence, possessed of clear comprehension and endowed with mindfulness, the yogi who delights in meditation—to that Buddha I bow. 320.
Freed from all defilements, always possessing a compassionate heart;
Freed from all reproach, I bow down to that Buddha.
(321) Free from anger in every respect, a treasury of compassion in every respect, liberated from all that is blameworthy—I bow down to that Buddha. (322)
Completely freed from all afflictions, liberated from bonds in every way, and released from the thorns of doubt and desire—I bow down to that Buddha. 323.
Completely detached from all undertakings, with a mind always and ever composed;
Liberated from shaking and trembling, I bow down to that Buddha.
(324) Completely liberated from all conditioned things, well-seen in the unconditioned, liberated from restlessness and remorse—I bow down to that Buddha. (325)
Freed from all calamities, with a mind unattached and joyful, liberated from the entire cycle of wandering existence—to that Buddha I bow. 326.
Released from all clinging and freed from all intoxications;
Empty of all sense-bases— bowing my head, I pay homage to that Buddha.
Liberated from all snares, with a mind perfectly serene,
freed from all conceits and underlying tendencies— bowing my head, I pay homage to that Buddha.
I bow to that Buddha who is forever free from all defilements, whose mind is eternally unstained, and who is liberated from all forms of ignorance.
He is free from the stirring of thoughts, and his mind is ever without fuel.
Completely liberated from all taints, I bow down to that Buddha.
(330) At all times with an unshakable mind, with a mind of firm liberation, and completely free from all distraction, I bow down to that Buddha. (331)
Freed from attachment to existence, liberated from the ocean of the three realms of being, completely released from all craving—him I bow down to as the Buddha. 332.
Released from the wheel of existence, well-tamed and thoroughly self-controlled;
With a mind that has reached the unconditioned, I bow down to that Buddha.
(333) Completely liberated from becoming, the seer who has vomited out worldly bait, you bear your final body—I bow down to that Buddha. (334)
Freed from all covetousness, contented, with a pure mind, liberated from the ocean of saṃsāra—I bow down to that Buddha. 335.
Liberated in every way and from everything, omniscient, the conqueror of all.
Subhadda was liberated from all bonds; I bow down to that Buddha.
Liberated from all obstacles, released from every bolt, and freed from all obstructions—I bow down to that Buddha.
Freed from all torment, cool and with a tranquil mind, liberated from the fire of craving for existence—to that Buddha I bow. 338.
Freed from crookedness, freed from the mire, free from bonds, with a liberated mind.
Always free from affliction, I bow down to that Buddha. 339.
In every way free from doubt, free from trembling, and confident;
like a fire freed from smoke, I bow down to that Buddha. 340.
Always free from harshness, entirely free from malice, and everywhere completely free—I bow down to that Buddha. 341.
Straight-minded, well-straightened in mind, even-minded, and even in conduct;
With a mind of wisdom and a mind of steadfastness, I bow down to that Buddha. 342.
With a mind free from greed and hatred, with a beautiful mind unattached, with a mind free from delusion and a mind of wisdom, I bow down to that Buddha. 343.
With a virtuous mind, a pure mind, a secure mind, and endowed with mindfulness;
with a beautiful mind, an auspicious mind—to that Buddha I bow.
With a mind of Dhamma, a mind of welfare, a resolute mind, and the supreme mind.
With a mind of modesty and a mind of glory, I bow down to that Buddha.
With a mind of welfare and a mind of happiness, with a virtuous mind and compassion;
with a mind of joy and a mind of coolness, I bow down to that Buddha.
With supremely pure mind, with liberated mind, the best of ascetics;
with restrained mind and well-composed mind—to that Buddha I bow.
With joyful mind and gladdened mind, with the most excellent and most perfect mind.
With a contented mind and joyful, I bow down to that Buddha.
(348) Mindful, self-restrained, possessed of clear comprehension and energy, with a noble mind and endowed with wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha. (349)
With a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of compassion, a mind of mercy, and one who is perfectly pure;
rejoicing with a mind of gentleness—to that Buddha I bow down. 350.
With a mind of truth, a mind of suchness, a mind of excellent virtue, and possessed of moral discipline;
With a mind free from greed, a pure mind—to that Buddha I bow.
With a mind free from hatred, cleansed; with a mind free from delusion, unattached;
with a stainless mind, detached—to that Buddha I bow.
Divine-minded, capable-minded, tamed-minded, the One of Ten Powers;
Delighting in the state of capability, the Capable One—I bow down to that Buddha.
Wisdom-minded, intelligence-minded, science-minded, the possessor of the wealth of science;
One whose mind is wisdom, one whose mind is final knowledge—I bow down to that Buddha.
(354) One whose mind is radiant, one whose mind is luminous, one whose mind is bright, the giver of light;
one whose mind is lovely, one whose mind is patient—I bow down to that Buddha. (355)
I bow down to that Buddha who is stainless, whose mind is pure white, whose mind is serene and gentle, who is holy, and whose mind is purified. (356) He whose mind is swift, whose mind is powerful,
whose mind is steadfast, and who is confident.
With a steady mind, with a firm mind—I bow down to that Buddha.
(357) With a mind of vitality, with a mind of splendor, with a warrior’s mind, unwavering;
with a fearless mind, unshakable—I bow down to that Buddha. (358)
Skilled, with a mind of noble wisdom, with a restrained and self-controlled mind;
with a serene and tranquil mind—to that Buddha I bow down.
With an auspicious mind and a mind set on liberation, the most excellent of all, the supreme among beings.
With a mind full of joy and at peace, I bow down to that Buddha.
(360) With a peaceful mind, a tamed mind, a mind of mastery, one who has lived the holy life;
with a pure mind and a radiant mind, I bow down to that Buddha. (361)
With guarded mind, liberated mind, serene mind, and upright mind;
with joyful mind and pure mind—I bow down to that Buddha.
With peaceful mind, ever-peaceful, the sage who is always contented.
Restraint in all things, O Lord—I bow down to that Buddha.
(363) Desiring emptiness, thirsting for emptiness, with passion emptied, with dust emptied;
with will emptied, with delight emptied—I bow down to that Buddha. (364)
Empty of malice, empty of anger, empty of burning passion, empty of turbidity;
empty of wrath, empty of irritation—I bow down to that Buddha.
Empty of worldly ties, empty of attachment to the world, empty of lust, empty of delight in the world;
Empty of delight, empty of craving— I bow down to that Buddha.
Empty of all the afflictions of existence, empty of the great darkness of delusion,
entirely empty of ignorance— I bow down to that Buddha.
Empty of the fetter of delight, having relinquished all attachments,
with the supreme goal attained in his hand— to that Buddha I bow. Empty of agitation,
empty of fueling, empty of craving, and empty of evil.
Free from craving, free from grasping—I bow down to that Buddha.
(369) He has reached the end, attained the end, reached the further shore, gone beyond to the other side;
he has reached the limit, attained the limit—I bow down to that Buddha. (370)
Attained to security, gone to security; attained to the highest, gone to the highest;
attained to bliss, gone to bliss—I bow down to that Buddha. 371.
Attained to the state of peace, attained to the eternal, attained to complete purity, the Sovereign.
Having reached the path and having reached the fruit, I bow down to that Buddha. 372.
Having reached the essence, gone to the further shore, reached the ultimate limit, and attained excellence;
having attained complete purity, I bow down to that Buddha. 373.
Stainless, having attained purity, having attained Nibbāna, free from defilement;
stainless, having attained the Deathless—to that Buddha I bow. 374.
Attained to the Dhamma, a practitioner of the Dhamma, attained to skillfulness, the Absolute One (Kevalin).
Having attained the supramundane, you are worthy of honor; I bow down to that Buddha.
(375) Having attained insight, having attained wisdom, and having attained supreme enlightenment;
having attained peace and having attained happiness—I bow down to that Buddha. (376)
I bow to that Buddha who has attained the Dhamma, attained enlightenment, attained the Path, and attained the Fruit; who has attained the deathless and attained his goal.
He has attained the ultimate truth, attained security, and attained peace.
Having reached the goal, having attained the goal, I bow down to that Buddha.
(378) Having reached the noble state, established in the goal, certain of the goal, one who has reached the destruction of the goal;
having reached the supramundane Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. (379)
Having attained knowledge, having attained wisdom, having attained the certainty of the Dhamma;
having attained the infinite, having attained the end—I bow down to that Buddha.
Having attained purity, having attained supernormal power, having attained the state of the ultimate goal.
I bow down to that Buddha whose Dhamma possesses the meaning of skillfulness. 381.
He who has attained, whose complexion is like a bowl, whose fame is attained, whose glory is attained, and who is renowned for having attained supernormal powers—I bow down to that Buddha. 382.
All eons have been exhausted for you;
liberated and majestic, you have reached the further shore of the flood of saṃsāra—I bow down to that Buddha. 383.
You have attained the method, you have attained mastery, and you have reached the perfection of realization.
To that Buddha who has perfectly realized the way out [of suffering], I bow down. 384.
The Venerable One, the breaker of the burden, the shatterer of worldly enjoyments, who has crossed the great ocean of existence—to that Buddha, I bow down. 385.
Having fulfilled, without exception, the difficult requisites for enlightenment, you attained the knowledge of omniscience; I bow down to that Buddha.
386. You have attained peace, become peace itself, and become cooled in every respect.
Having attained supreme happiness, I bow down to that Buddha. 387. One whose wealth is wisdom, one who is devoted to wisdom, one who relies on wisdom, one whose abode is wisdom;
one for whom wisdom is the pillar, one for whom wisdom is the arrow— I bow down to that Buddha. 388.
With wisdom as his raft, with wisdom as his protection, with wisdom as his security, with wisdom as his courtyard;
seeking wisdom, longing for wisdom—to that Buddha I bow down. 389.
One who has laid down the burden, who has done what was to be done, who has perfected the higher knowledges and reached fulfillment.
I bow down to that Buddha who has brought all things to their final completion. 390.
Guarded in mind, guarded in speech, guarded in body—the supreme guardian;
whose actions are guarded and whose nature is guarded—I bow down to that Buddha. 391.
Guarded in mind, tamed in mind, with a peaceful and restrained mind;
liberated in mind, tranquil in mind—to that Buddha I bow. 392.
Well-guarded in his faculties, well-protected, a leader who has realized the goal for himself.
Endowed with abundant wisdom, I bow down to that Buddha.
(393) Guarded in body, guarded in speech, and guarded in mind—He whose self is well-guarded, the Master who guards all his faculties, I bow down to that Buddha. (394)
Steadfast-hearted and courageous, restrained and with a controlled mind, guarding his sense-faculties and guarding his thoughts—to that Buddha I bow. 395.
Endowed with fortitude, endowed with wisdom, endowed with policy, and possessed of the right method.
Connected with the path, connected with the fruit—to that Buddha I bow.
Attained the path, attained the goal, attained the end, attained the way;
attained the ultimate truth—to that Buddha I bow.
I bow to that Buddha who has attained what is desirable, attained perfection, attained coolness, and attained bliss; who has attained the Nibbāna so difficult to find.
(398) He has attained the Dhamma, attained the goal, attained liberation, and attained suchness.
I bow down to that Buddha who attained the twenty pāramīs through his practice.
399. I bow down to that Buddha who attained peace, attained patience, attained beauty, and attained glory; who attained splendor and attained fame. 400.
Having attained what is difficult to attain, having attained what is possible to attain, having attained everything, and having attained power;
having attained the auspicious which is so very hard to see—I bow down to that Buddha.
401. Having attained purity, having attained awakening, having attained supernormal power, and having attained the treasure-trove;
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the six supernormal powers (chaḷabhiññā). 402.
Having attained what is auspicious and wholesome, having attained joy, having attained happiness, and having reached the ocean of the Deathless (amata)—I bow down to that Buddha. 403.
Having attained security from bondage, having found safety, having found the certain;
the Hero who has obtained the Ten Powers—to that Buddha I bow.
404. Having attained enlightenment, having attained knowledge, having attained wisdom, having attained the method;
Attained to wisdom, attained to true knowledge—I bow down to that Buddha.
(405) Attained to sublime understanding, attained to steadfastness, having attained the perfection of liberation;
attained to the supreme state of final peace—I bow down to that Buddha. (406)
Purified and sanctified has he been attained;
attained is the highest blessing. Attained is the supreme security—him, the Buddha, I bow down to. 407.
Exalted and absolute has he been attained; attained is the excellent liberation in every respect.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the end of the endless cycle of suffering.

408. I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the seven factors of enlightenment, who has attained supernormal powers in every respect, and who has attained the destruction of the craving for existence. 409.
Attained by the perfectly pure path, attained through truth, incomparable;
attained through the fulfilled Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow.
Attained through complete fullness of thorough knowledge, attained through final knowledge, the most supreme of all.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā), 411.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained manifest liberation, who is preeminent in having gained the six higher knowledges (chaḷabhiññā), and who has attained perfect peace. 412.
Having attained the truths as they truly are, having attained suchness in every respect,
having attained universal equanimity— I bow down to that Buddha.
Having attained the stainless eye, he is an ocean of pure knowledge.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the Dhamma of subtle meaning.
414. I bow down to that Buddha who has attained steadfastness, attained speed, attained tranquility, and possesses majesty; who has attained the supramundane truths. 415.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained steadfastness, attained purity, attained complete purification, and possesses purity;
who has attained ambrosia, is highly wise, has attained excellence, has attained auspiciousness, and has attained the supreme.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained what was to be attained, attained what is blessed, attained the highest state, and attained what is beautiful.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained contentment in all things.
(417) I bow down to that Buddha who has reached the shore, reached the further bank, reached the essence, and attained the fruit;
who has attained the supreme auspiciousness. (418)
Attained by rays, attained by splendor, attained by vital energy, attained by radiance;
attained by the highest and supreme luster—I bow down to that Buddha.
Attained through praise and accomplishment, distinguished and renowned throughout the world.
I bow down to that Buddha who has obtained worship and praise. 420.
I bow down to that Buddha, the life of the world, who is liberated from the darkness of delusion, who has obtained light, and who has obtained immeasurable radiance. 421.
The Teacher is skilled and free from taints, expert in what is action and what is not action;
having gone beyond all actions, I bow down to that Buddha. 422.
He is skilled in the wholesome and skilled in the unwholesome;
Perfectly endowed with the wholesome, I bow down to that Buddha. 423.
Skilled in the Dhamma and skilled also in what is not Dhamma, having reached the further shore of all phenomena, I bow down to that Buddha. 424.
Skilled in merit and skilled in demerit,
having transcended both evil and merit— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in the path and skilled in what is not the path, I bow to that Buddha.
He eradicated the supreme path; I bow down to that Buddha.
(426) Skilled in both happiness and skilled in suffering, seeing the ultimate bliss—I bow down to that Buddha. (427)
Skilled in what is desirable and skilled in what is undesirable,
he has pointed out the supreme goal— I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in the finite and skilled in the infinite...
I bow down to that Buddha, the witness of infinite radiance. 429.
Skilled in the mortal and skilled in the immortal, having reached the ocean of the immortal—I bow down to that Buddha. 430.
Skilled in the permanent and skilled in the impermanent,
you proclaimed the truth of permanence— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in existence and skilled in non-existence...
You have utterly shattered existence; I bow down to you, that Buddha.
Skilled in passion and likewise skilled in the absence of passion, you have cleansed away all passion; I bow down to you, that Buddha.
Skilled in hatred and skilled in non-hatred, you have destroyed every form of hatred; I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in delusion and skilled in non-delusion...
Having transcended all delusion, I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in both enmity and the absence of enmity,
having transcended all enmity, I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in defilement and skilled in the absence of defilement, he has incinerated all defilements—I bow down to that Buddha. 437.
Skilled in darkness and skilled in light;
He illuminates the light in the world—I bow down to that Buddha.
(438) Skilled in what is free from deceit, and skilled in what is not deceitful;
free from guile and free from affliction—I bow down to that Buddha. (439)
Skilled in attachment, and skilled in non-attachment;
liberated from all attachments—to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in feeling, and skilled in the absence of feeling;
Transcending all sensation— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in exertion and skilled in non-exertion,
having relinquished all exertion— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in the *ālaya* and skilled in that which is without *ālaya*, liberated from all *ālayas*—to that Buddha I bow. 443.
Skilled in the object of perception and skilled in that which is without an object of perception...
He has transcended all objects of perception; I bow down to that Buddha.
(444) Skilled in craving and skilled in the absence of craving, he has torn asunder the net of craving; I bow down to that Buddha. (445)
Skilled in pride and skilled in contempt,
equal toward both pride and contempt— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in desire and skilled in the absence of desire,
I bow down to that Buddha who has completely exhausted all desires. 447.
Skilled in both anger and the absence of anger, extinguished by the fire of all anger—I bow down to that Buddha. 448.
Skilled in anger, and skilled in the absence of anger;
he who extinguished the fire of anger—to that Buddha I bow. 449.
Skilled in desire, and skilled in the absence of desire;
I bow down to that Buddha who has severed all desire for existence. 450.
He is skilled in regard to greed, and also skilled in regard to the absence of greed;
unstained by the craving for greed, I bow down to that Buddha. 451.
Skilled in sorrow and skilled in the absence of sorrow,
he has extracted the dart of grief— I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in affection and skilled in the absence of affection...
Completely free from all attachments, I bow down to that Buddha.
(453) Skilled in both agitation and non-agitation, with all agitations of karma exhausted, I bow down to that Buddha. (454)

Having attained the eternal and the inexhaustible, I bow down to that Buddha. 456.
Skilled in the world and skilled in the end of the world, having realized that which transcends the world, I bow down to that Buddha. 457.
Skilled in what is pure and skilled in what is impure,
he purified the path to purity— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in the right time and skilled in the wrong time...
Kālānusārī taught [the Dhamma]; I bow down to that Buddha. 459.
Skilled in sophistry and skilled in the absence of sophistry, liberated from sophistry in every way—I bow down to that Buddha. 460.
Skilled in the joyful and skilled in the sorrowful,
the noble one who is joyful in every respect— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in the wheel of the world and skilled in the wheel of Dhamma.
You shattered the wheel of the world; I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in this shore and skilled in the further shore, having gone beyond the terrible flood, I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in awakening, and skilled even in that which is difficult to awaken;
you have awakened to everything in every way—I bow down to that Buddha.
464. Skilled in yoga, and skilled in security as well;
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the security from bondage (yogakkhema).
465. Skilled in the turbid and skilled in the non-turbid, he has cleared away all turbidity; I bow down to that Buddha. 466.
Skilled in doubt and skilled in the absence of doubt,
liberated from doubt in every respect— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in timidity and skilled in fearlessness;
Endowed with the knowledge of self-confidence, I bow to that Buddha.
(468) Skilled in both the mutable and the immutable, he suppressed all mutations; I bow to that Buddha. (469)
Skilled in delusion and skilled in non-delusion,
liberated from all delusion— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in distress and skilled in non-distress...
I bow to that Buddha who brings an end to all torments. 471.
I bow to that Buddha who is skilled regarding aversion and skilled regarding non-aversion, and who is empty of the perception of aversion. 472.
Skilled in that which has taints, and skilled in that which is without taints;
with all taints utterly destroyed—I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in the virtuous, and skilled in the unvirtuous as well;
Endowed with every excellent quality, I bow down to that Buddha.
(474) Skilled in what is wholesome and skilled in what is unwholesome, having attained the goal of the wholesome, I bow down to that Buddha. (475)
To him of vast wisdom, powerful, skilled in what is the path and what is not the path, who has attained the Dhamma of the ultimate goal—to that Buddha I bow. 476.
Skilled in mental tranquility, skilled in meditative absorption and concentration...
Having attained the meditative absorptions, I bow down to that Buddha. 477.
Skilled in the path and knowing the path, skilled in the Dhamma and knowing the Dhamma, skilled in the supreme and knowing the supreme—I bow down to that Buddha. 478.
Skilled in clear comprehension, skilled in right mindfulness,
skilled in the foundations of mindfulness— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in the seven factors of enlightenment, skilled in all the analytical expositions;
Skilled in true knowledge, possessed of the threefold lore—I bow down to that Buddha.
480. Skilled in the liberation of mind, skilled in the liberation through wisdom;
having attained liberation in both ways—I bow down to that Buddha. 481.
Skilled in the bases of psychic power, skilled in discerning the minds of others,
endowed with the six direct knowledges— to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in the immeasurables, one who has gone beyond the Eightfold Path.
Having attained liberation through the complete cessation [of defilements], I bow down to that Buddha. 483.
Skilled in the fixed order of the Dhamma, skilled in the nature of phenomena (dhammatā), and skilled in the stability of the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. 484.
Endowed with restraint of body, skilled in restraint of mind, and guarded by restraint of speech—to that Buddha I bow. 485.
The eldest in the world, the best in the world, the eldest in the three worlds, the possessor of the threefold knowledge;
Foremost among men, most distinguished—I bow down to that Buddha. 486.
Most excellent, established in the sublime Dhamma, rightly subduing all;
free from attachment, detached—I bow down to that Buddha. 487.
Eldest of all, best of all, the leader of all, the guide of all;
the protector of all, the lord of all—to that Buddha I bow.
Conqueror of death, conqueror of Māra, the destroyer of Māra’s realm.
He destroyed the snare of Māra; I bow down to that Buddha. 489.
The conqueror of death, the slayer of Māra, the destroyer of the realm of death;
he destroyed the snare of death; I bow down to that Buddha. 490.
Victor over Māra, victor over Death, the destroyer of the realm of the End-Maker;
he has trampled the field of death—I bow down to that Buddha. 491.
The Hero, full of valor, the crusher of Māra’s army;
Having crossed over death and conquered death, I bow down to that Buddha. 492.
You crushed the illusion of Māra, you are the slayer of the deluding Māra;
you are the one who tramples upon the intoxication of Māra—I bow down to that Buddha. 493.
Powerful, he crushed Māra; strong, he subdued Death;
that Nāga who devours Namuci—that Buddha, I bow down to him.
494. The Great Victor crushed the army of the wicked Māra’s forces.
He has attained supreme bliss; I bow down to that Buddha.
(495) Victorious over evil, victorious over merit, victorious over the self, and having conquered pride;
victorious over doubt, victorious over suspicion—I bow down to that Buddha. (496)
I bow down to that Buddha who has conquered delusion, conquered deceit, and conquered hypocrisy;
who is unconquered by Māra, who has conquered stinginess, and who has conquered craving.
497. He has conquered anger, conquered lust, conquered greed, and conquered delight.
I bow down to that Buddha who has conquered craving, who has conquered passion. 498.

I bow down to that Buddha who has conquered enmity, who has conquered attachment, who has conquered pride, who has conquered intoxication, who has conquered illness, and who has conquered longing. 499.
The hero who is victorious at all times, the All-Conqueror, the supreme ascetic;
the giver of security, the Lord of Security—to that Buddha I bow down. 500.
The Conqueror of All, the Master of All, the auspicious one of victory over all.
Victorious over all, the lion of the Sakyas—to that Buddha I bow down.
Subdued in body, subdued in mind, subdued in negligence, subdued by wisdom;
with subdued exertion and subdued composure—to that Buddha I bow down.
With tusks like ivory, with tusks as white as ivory, with tusks that inspire awe, with tusks that strike fear;
with tusks that terrify, with tusks that are formidable—I bow down to that Buddha.
With tusks free from blemish, with tusks free from fault, with tusks worthy of praise, with tusks like ivory.
With burning teeth, with blazing teeth, I bow down to that Buddha.
Exerting himself rightly, valiant, with a mind of great prowess, he strove as the conqueror of Māra; I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in right effort, restrained and exceedingly self-controlled, perfected in the perfections—to that Buddha I bow. 506.
Possessing shame and fear of wrongdoing, ardent and well-tamed, exceedingly self-controlled.
The best of the Śākyas, the eldest of all—to that Buddha I bow.
Possessor of the ten powers, firm, wise, conqueror of the unconquerable;
the bull among men, the hero—to that Buddha I bow.
The supreme among bipeds, the tamer, the tamed one of firm exertion;
free from hatred and knowing hatred—him I bow to, the Buddha.
509. He who exerts effort, strives, initiates energy, and is courageous.
You fulfilled the perfections; I bow down to that Buddha. 510.
Radiant, having reached the perfections, striving and resolute;
you defeated Māra the Evil One; I bow down to that Buddha. 511.
Endowed with the power of Java, a hero whose crest is valor, a steadfast bearer of fortitude—I bow down to that Buddha.
His valor is difficult to overcome; his prowess is untiring.
I bow down to that Buddha who has reached the unfathomable nectar of immortality. 513.
I bow down to that Buddha who is endowed with mindfulness and diligence, who has mastered the right exertions, and who possesses the vision of the Noble Ones. 514.
Endowed with right effort, having reached the further shore of the right exertions, having attained all goals and accomplished his purpose—to that Buddha I bow down. 515.
A hero who has conquered the battle, a victor who has overcome enmity.
Wise, the bearer of the burden of men—I bow down to that Buddha.
(516) The Bull among Men fulfilled all the perfections through his exertion;
liberated from birth and death—I bow down to that Buddha. (517)
Vigor and exertion, the abandoner of evil deeds, the one who exerts effort and applies skillful means—to that Buddha I bow. 518.
For the sake of the welfare and benefit of all beings, he strove and exerted himself.
He sought the liberation of Muttāyana; I bow down to that Buddha.
(519) The fearless lion among men completely cut through the cycle of existence;
having fully attained the supreme goal, I bow down to that Buddha. (520)
Delusion destroyed, deceit destroyed, hypocrisy destroyed, pride destroyed;
conceit destroyed, Māra destroyed—I bow down to that Buddha. 521.
Destroyers of hypocrisy, destroyers of the womb, destroyers of the cycle of existence, the Arhats.
I bow down to that Buddha who has destroyed the seeds [of rebirth] and destroyed all afflictions;
522. I bow down to that Buddha who has completely destroyed the conduit to existence, whose mind is liberated from the conditioned, and who has destroyed ignorance in every respect. 523.
With self-restrained body, self-controlled mind, with passions stilled and composed;
with self-liberated and dispassionate heart—to that Buddha I bow. 524.
He who has transcended evil, transcended merit, transcended the "I," and transcended possessiveness;
I bow down to that Buddha who has cut through doubt, who has cut through uncertainty.
525. I bow down to that Buddha who has cut through the eon, who has cut through time, who has completely cut through the defilements; who has cut through the root, who has cut through the stake. 526.
Perishable is birth, perishable is death; perishable is the world, perishable is existence;
perishable is dissolution, perishable is the flood—to that Buddha I bow.
