Perishable is agitation, perishable is suffering; perishable is the dart, perishable is the thicket.
Destroyer of conceit, destroyer of craving—I bow down to that Buddha.
(528) Shatterer of hatred, shatterer of malice, shatterer of sensual desire, shatterer of darkness;
shatterer of views, shatterer of suffering—I bow down to that Buddha. (529)
I bow down to that Buddha who shatters enjoyment, shatters sorrow, shatters disease, and shatters passion;
who shatters the stake, shatters the arrow, shatters sloth, shatters torpor, shatters bondage, and shatters the yoke.
530. He who shatters arrogance, shatters dullness, shatters fetters, and shatters the crossbar.
I bow down to that Buddha who breaks the beginning of [suffering],
who is free from grasping, who has broken fear, who has broken affliction, who has broken pride,
who has broken negligence, who delights in breaking [the fetters], and who is free from desire. 531–532.
I bow down to that Buddha who has shattered remorse, shattered [the fetters], shattered the assembly, and shattered the taints; who has demolished pride and overweening pride.
He is the shatterer of the arrow, the shatterer of the stake, the shatterer of the root, and the shatterer of impurity. 533.
I bow down to that Buddha who has shattered all bonds of existence.
(534) The destruction of the eon, the destruction of time, the destruction of defilements in every way;
the destruction of the root, the destruction of the stake—I bow down to that Buddha. (535)
The destruction of the two, the destruction of the two, the destruction of desire, free from pride;

the destruction of views, the destruction of suffering—to that Buddha I bow. 536. One whose anger is destroyed, whose resentment is destroyed, whose afflictions are destroyed, and whose hypocrisy is destroyed.
I bow down to that Buddha who has exhausted the world, who has exhausted the realm of existence.
537. I bow down to that Buddha who has exhausted greed, who has exhausted lust, who has exhausted anger, whose strife is ended; who has exhausted hardship, who has exhausted desire. 538.
With lust destroyed, with hatred destroyed, with delusion destroyed, with existence destroyed;
with pride destroyed, with hypocrisy destroyed—to that Buddha I bow.
With greed destroyed, with avarice destroyed, with desire destroyed, and with the taints destroyed.
I bow down to that Buddha whose exertion has ceased and whose delusion is exhausted. 540.
I bow down to that Buddha whose craving has ceased, whose seed is exhausted, who is masterful with no desire for rebirth, whose thirst is ended, and whose breaking [of bonds] is finished. 541.
Free from fear of destruction, free from anxiety of destruction, free from doubt regarding destruction, free from the turmoil of destruction;
longing for destruction, intent upon destruction—to that Buddha I bow. 542.
Free from thirst for destruction, free from greed for destruction, free from the arrow of destruction, free from the barrenness of destruction.
The ender of craving for existence, the ender of disease—I bow down to that Buddha.
543. The ender of trepidation, the ender of fear, the ender of terror, the ender of dread;
the ender of doubt, the ender of distress—I bow down to that Buddha. 544.
Associated with destruction, the state of destruction, the abode of destruction, the grasp of destruction;
the thorn of destruction, the root of destruction—to that Buddha I bow. 545.
The destruction of "I," the destruction of "mine," the destruction of all conditioned things in every respect.
Having attained the destruction of defilements, I bow down to that Buddha.
(546) Empty of craving, empty of passion, empty of delight, empty of attachment;
empty of desire, empty of joy—I bow down to that Buddha. (547)
Empty of anger, empty of hatred, empty of malice, empty of burning;
empty of curses, empty of fever—bowing my head, I pay homage to that Buddha.
Empty of wrath, empty of rage, empty of affliction, empty of deceit.
Empty of enemies, empty of foes—him, the Buddha, I pay homage.
(549) Empty of birth, empty of death, empty of the world, empty of existence;
the Sugata who delights in emptiness—him, the Buddha, I pay homage. (550)
Empty of calamities, empty of fears, empty of terrors, and empty of fear itself;
entirely empty of cowardice—to that Buddha I bow. 551.
Empty of knots, empty of ropes, and entirely empty of bonds.
The view of emptiness, the guide to emptiness—I bow to that Buddha.
Empty of arrows, empty of thorns, empty of roots, empty of stains;
empty of all underlying tendencies—I bow to that Buddha.
Empty of all burning, empty of all anxiety in every way;
empty of thirst, empty of fear—to that Buddha I bow. 554.
Empty of longing, empty of envy, empty of craving, and empty of the five [fetters].
Empty of desire, empty of bondage—I bow down to that Buddha.
(555) Empty of evil, empty of merit, empty of "I," and empty of "mine";
empty of doubt, empty of suspicion—I bow down to that Buddha. (556)
Having abandoned all karma, generous, free from longing in every respect, and in every way detached from social ties—to that Buddha I bow. 557.
He who has abandoned hatred, abandoned malice, abandoned anger, and is free from fuel for rebirth;
One who has abandoned anger and abandoned wrath— to that Buddha I bow.
One who has abandoned all royal enjoyments, the one who brings one out of the great flood, the seer of the Dhamma of the ultimate meaning— to that Buddha I bow.
Free from anger, free from defilements, free from attachment, free from taints;
free from evil, free from distress—to that Buddha I bow down.
(560) Thus fallen away from fear, fallen away from trembling, fallen away from trepidation, and free from all dread.
Freed from burning, freed from burning, I bow down to that Buddha.
(561) Having abandoned all, having conquered all, the giver of all, the one who has gone beyond all;
he who is full in every way, the relinquisher of all—I bow down to that Buddha. (562)
Free from attachment, free from affliction, free from longing, and free from blemish;
with a mind always unattached—to that Buddha, I bow down. 563.
Free from envy, free from expectation, free from desire, and free from striving;
Taintless and free from longing, I bow down to that Buddha.
(564) Like space in wisdom, unstained like the wind, he who dwelt without dependence—I bow down to that Buddha. (565)
Aroused in energy, ardent, striving, and resolute;
unwearied and untiring—to that Buddha I bow. 566.
The Teacher is peerless, the eldest, the most excellent of all, the instructor.
He has realized the noble Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha.
(567) He has satisfied the world with the Deathless, raining down the cloud of Dhamma;
he has brought comfort like the moon— I bow down to that Buddha. (568)
Unshakable, fearless, undaunted, and free from distress;
to that Buddha who is brave and without trembling, I pay homage. 569.
Unselfish, free from deceit, without loathing, and not cruel;
Unangered and not crooked—him, the Buddha, I bow down to. 570.
Without covetousness, without envy, without guile, without greed;
blameless and sober—him, the Buddha, I bow down to. 571.
Free from immodesty, free from resentment, untroubled and undeluded;
free from backbiting and free from hatred—I bow to that Buddha.
572. Free from anger and not wicked, devoid of longing and non-malicious;
Free from anger, free from deceit—I bow down to that Buddha. 573.
Unshaken, immovable, without enmity, and fearless from any quarter;
always devoid of trembling—I bow down to that Buddha. 574.
Free from pride, free from harshness, unagitated, and not prone to anger;
not easily provoked and without malice—to that Buddha I bow. 575.
Without roughness and without agitation, without bitterness and without deceit;
Free from conceit in this present life, I bow down to that Buddha.
(576) Without expectation, without attachment, unclinging, and unperturbed;
unstained and without support, I bow down to that Buddha. (577)
The Sage, the supreme minister, whose self is fully extinguished,
the ascetic, purified, perfectly awakened— I bow down to that Buddha.
He has pulled out the arrow, is free from dust, possesses the eye of wisdom, and is without taints.
Anomadassī, free from debt— to that Buddha I bow. The foundation of meaning, the one who has reached the goal,
the one who has attained the further shore of boundless meaning,
the ultimate one skilled in meaning— to that Buddha I bow.
Having attained the noble paths, wise in the meaning of the goal, you liberated beings from their bonds—I bow down to that Buddha. 581.
With a mind unattached and undaunted, always possessing a mind free from clinging;
The Protector who delights in heedfulness—to that Buddha I bow.
(582) With a mind unattached and free from affliction, in whom no longing exists;
undefiled and without guile—to that Buddha I bow. (583)
With a mind of equanimity, immovable, upright through the destruction of clinging;
having broken through, free from craving—I bow down to that Buddha. 584.
Having reached the perfection of direct knowledge, possessing supreme wisdom, he has gone beyond.
I bow down to that Buddha who is liberated without clinging. 585.
I bow down to that Buddha who is unopposed, unattached, who has attained peace, who is immeasurable, and who has reached the deathless. 586.
Desiring nothing, free from clinging, supreme;
without craving and without hatred—to that Buddha I bow. 587.
With exceeding virtue, exceeding peace, and exceeding wisdom, O Worthy One!
Having attained the highest goal, you are supreme; I bow down to that Buddha. 588.
You have mastered higher virtue, higher consciousness, and higher wisdom;
you are one who looks with clear vision; I bow down to that Buddha. 589.
With self as island, with self as refuge, having oneself as lord and supreme protector, the ultimate pinnacle, the highest of beings—to that Buddha I bow. 590.
Free from longing, free from desire, free from passion, and without expectation;
Free from craving, free from greed—bowing my head, I pay homage to that Buddha.
(591) Without longing, without fuel, a seer whose thirst has not grown;
with passion cut off, unattached—bowing my head, I pay homage to that Buddha. (592)
With lust destroyed, with hatred destroyed, with delusion destroyed, with pride destroyed;
with anger destroyed, with resentment destroyed—to that Buddha I bow down.
With craving destroyed, with attachment destroyed, with desire destroyed, with grasping destroyed.
Hope is lost, fear is lost—to that Buddha I bow.
Doubt is destroyed, suspicion is destroyed, pride is destroyed, delusion is destroyed;
deceit is destroyed, ignorance is destroyed—to that Buddha I bow.
Devoid of guile, unbounded, upright, and exceedingly renowned;
with a mind beyond compare and free from blemish—I bow down to that Buddha. 596.
He who perceives the welfare, who acts for the welfare, who proclaims the welfare, and who accomplishes the welfare;
Desiring my welfare and being well-pleased, I bow down to that Buddha. 597.
Wondrous and marvelous, a speaker of the heart and an instructor!
You have well-expounded the supreme path; I bow down to that Buddha. 598.
Untainted, stainless, pure, and unerring;
free from remorse and without doubt—to that Buddha I bow. 599.
Completely victorious, a hero, fearless, and the giver of fearlessness;
Unperturbed and fearless, I bow down to that Buddha.
(600) Equanimous, peaceful, a seer whose taints are exhausted, unattached and unfettered—I bow down to that Buddha. (601)
One who acts for the welfare, who brings about welfare, who seeks welfare, who delights in welfare;
one who knows welfare, who speaks of welfare—to that Buddha I bow. 602.
The unsurpassed, the sorrowless, the bull, the preeminent among seers;
Of unsurpassed name, unsurpassed—him, the Buddha, I bow down to.
(603) With a heart free from lust, with a mind unassailed;
dispassionate and immovable—him, the Buddha, I bow down to. (604)
Free from fear, free from affliction, free from longing, free from blemish;
free from craving, free from wavering—to that Buddha I bow down. 605.
Knower of meaning, knower of the goal, skilled in meaning, possessor of meaning;
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the goal of skillfulness.
(606) Unwavering, unshakable, like a lion, undaunted;
unshaken and fearless—I bow down to that Buddha. (607)
Possessing nothing, grasping at nothing,
knowing the deathless and immersed in the deathless, having attained the supreme fruit— to that Buddha I bow.
Having bestowed immeasurable favor, he is the giver of the timeless Dhamma.
The Protector who is of ultimate benefit—I bow down to that Buddha.
(609) Unstained by the world, like a lotus by water;
with a mind free from attachment and devoid of self-identity—I bow down to that Buddha. (610)
The seer who has pulled out the thorn, who has lifted the crossbar, who is upright, undisturbed, and untiring—to that Buddha I bow. 611.
He is free from greed, his mind is unstained, and he is a piercer of the danger [of suffering].
To you who are of natural character and resolute in purpose, I bow down to that Buddha.
612. Supreme in merit, supreme in wisdom, you were the foremost and the crest-jewel;
having attained the supreme path, I bow down to that Buddha. 613.
Foremost in range, foremost in conduct, supreme in purpose, supreme in teaching;
supreme in knowledge, supreme in speech—to that Buddha I bow.
Foremost in wisdom, established in the supreme, perfected in the supreme, he moves with the supreme.
Foremost being, lord of the foremost—I bow down to that Buddha.
(615) Foremost ascetic, supreme in the world, foremost in wisdom, the one who has reached the foremost path;
you have revealed the foremost Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. (616)
Having attained the supreme Dhamma, the proclaimer of the supreme Dhamma;
you destroyed the suffering of the states of woe—to that Buddha I bow.
617. The foremost person, the most excellent, supreme in wisdom, the preeminent one in knowledge;
One whose person is the Dhamma, whose path is the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow down.
(618) The supreme seer, the supreme observer, the proclaimer of the supreme path;
the supreme leader, the supreme perceiver—to that Buddha I bow down. (619)
To that Buddha, the lord of meditative absorption with infinite jhāna, the ocean of infinite wisdom, endowed with infinite intelligence—I pay homage. 620.
To the ocean of infinite knowledge, the sea of infinite wisdom;
I bow down to that Buddha, the ocean of infinite compassion.
(621) The most excellent of all, the highest among beings, the one of beautiful mind, the supreme ascetic;
the best of men, the supreme Victor—I bow down to that Buddha. (622)
He who has a virtuous friend is virtuous; he who has auspicious friends is auspicious.
He whose friend is the Dhamma is a giver of the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow.
He is established in the Dhamma and grounded in the Dhamma; he is established in wisdom and grounded in wisdom.
To him who is pure in view and pure in purpose, to that Buddha I bow down.
The witness of body, the witness of mind, the witness of Dhamma, the supreme witness;
the witness of feeling, the excellent witness—to that Buddha I bow down.
Quick in wisdom, most skillful, having attained peace, the lord of happiness;
doing what is beautiful, the one who is adept—to that Buddha I bow.
626. Foremost in virtue, foremost in pure mind, foremost in wisdom, and beautifully adorned;
Having reached the highest pinnacle, I bow down to that Buddha.
(627) Upariṭṭha, upright in conduct, exalted, bringing the deathless;
free from deceit and free from pride—I bow down to that Buddha. (628)
Little sorrow, little illness, little fear, little dread;
Little evil, little heat—him, the Buddha, I bow down to.
Little passion, little hatred, little malice, little fuel.
With little affliction and little anger, I bow down to that Buddha. 630.
Acting with ultimate compassion, with a mind of ultimate loving-kindness, peaceful and ultimately joyful, I bow down to that Buddha. 631.
Attained to solitude, having one protector, alone and without rival;
he alone in the entire world—I bow down to that Buddha. 632.
Incomparable, peerless, without a second, unsurpassed.
Immeasurable and peerless, I bow down to that Buddha.
Of incomparable vision, incomparable, without equal, matchless;
he who is unequaled and without likeness—I bow down to that Buddha.
Immeasurable and infinite, an ocean of immeasurable wisdom;
boundless and measureless—to that Buddha I bow down. 635.
Boundless, equal to the unequaled, incomparable, and of immeasurable virtues.
Incomparable and unfathomable, I bow down to that Buddha.
Unbounded, limitless, and beyond measure, the Supreme Victor;
immeasurable and peerless, I bow down to that Buddha.
There is no other wise person such as this;
experiencing absolute bliss, I bow down to that Buddha. 638.
He is the supreme bull, the peerless one, the incomparable individual.
I bow down to that Buddha who is alone, a solitary person. 639.
I bow down to that Buddha who is entirely empty of attachments, whose mind is in every way supreme, and who is always the same. 640.
You shattered the spit of evil, you are the cutter of the root of evil;
you have cut asunder the rope of evil—I bow down to that Buddha.
You have worn out the guide to evil, you are the destroyer of evil karma.
With all evil utterly exhausted, I bow down to that Buddha.
(642) Having uprooted evil, you have crossed to the further shore of the ocean of evil;
you have released the knot of evil—I bow down to that Buddha. (643)
Having crushed the wheel of evil, he set in motion the wheel of Dhamma;
he delivered many people—I bow down to that Buddha.
He exhausted his evil karma, having crossed to the further shore of the great flood of evil.
Having transcended all evil, I bow down to that Buddha. 645.
Having passed beyond all evil, having utterly removed all evil, and having completely uprooted all evil, I bow down to that Buddha. 646.
You distinguished yourself from evil, you who dispel the burning heat of wickedness;
you severed the craving for evil—I bow down to that Buddha. 647.
You are completely liberated from the state of evil, extinguished by the quenching of the fire of evil.
You liberated me from the bondage of evil; I bow down to that Buddha. 648.
You crushed the dart of evil; you are the one who tears asunder the wheel of evil;
you have exhausted the disease and sorrow of evil—I bow down to that Buddha. 649.
Freed from evil and delusion, dispelling the terror of evil,
you stilled the agitation of evil— I bow down to that Buddha.
You washed away the turbidity of darkness, cleansing the stains of evil.
He has purified all defilements; I bow down to that Buddha.
(651) Freed from the fever of evil, with the craving for evil liberated, and released from the torment of evil—I bow down to that Buddha. (652)
I bow down to that Buddha who has cut off the foundation of evil, who has shattered the obstacle of evil, and who has transcended the realm of evil.
He is the dispeller of both evil and merit, and the breaker of the bonds of existence.
To that Buddha who is the thorn among evil thorns, I bow down.
654. He has crushed all evil; he has abandoned all evil;
he has emerged from all evils—to that Buddha, I bow down. 655.
He has washed away all evil, he is one who loathes all evil;
liberated from all evils, I bow down to that Buddha. 656.
He has become free from all evil, he is the cleanser of all evil.
He has burned away all evil; I bow down to that Buddha.
(657) Having crossed over the ocean of evil, with the fetters of existence severed, and with rebirth utterly exhausted—I bow down to that Buddha. (658)
He washed away the mire of evil, carrying forth the stream of Dhamma;
he established the True Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
He completely cut off the heat of evil and cooled the heat of delusion.
He extinguished all suffering; I bow down to that Buddha.
(660) He who removes evil, he who removes torment, he who creates happiness, he who brings security, he who dwells in loving-kindness, the enemy of Māra—I bow down to that Buddha. (661)
To him whose fetters are completely exhausted, who has destroyed evil and torment, who has reached his final existence—to that Buddha I bow. 662.
To him who has entered the practice of the path, who has dispelled the burning heat of suffering;
To him whose evil and torment are utterly consumed, to that Buddha I bow.
To him whose merit and demerit are utterly consumed,
who has dispelled the dart of sorrow, and who is resolute in his striving— to that Buddha I bow.
To the One with Vision regarding all phenomena,
the destroyer of all evil, the slayer of all fetters— to that Buddha I bow down.
He has washed away all evil, the purifier of all defilements.
Stainless and pure in every respect, I bow down to that Buddha.
(666) He crushed all evil, more so than any host of ascetics;
he dispelled all torment— I bow down to that Buddha. (667)
The relinquishing of all acquisitions, the fading away of all cravings, he who has shattered all evil—I bow down to that Buddha. 668.
He who has gone beyond, who has reached the further shore, who dries up the stream of the taints;
I bow down to that Buddha who has abandoned all evil.
I bow down to that Buddha who has destroyed all taints through the total eradication of all delusion, and who has avoided all evil.
Having transcended all longing, extinguished the fire of all passion, and crushed out all evil—I bow down to that Buddha. 671.
Having crossed over the swamp of all sensual desires and existence, and having abandoned all worldly power and wealth;
To him who has cast off all evil and is free from defilement, to that Buddha I bow down.
672. To him who has transcended all hindrances, who has liberated himself from all snares, and who shattered Mara’s mirage, to that Buddha I bow down. 673.
The Master who grants refuge, the giver of protection,
the Teacher who bestows security— to that Buddha I bow.
He is skilled in the true, and likewise skilled in the untrue.
He proclaimed the Four Noble Truths; I bow down to that Buddha.
(675) Skilled in what is auspicious and skilled in what is inauspicious, seeing what is beneficial in all things—I bow down to that Buddha. (676)
Skilled in desire, skilled in the absence of desire,
and free from all longing— I bow down to that Buddha.
Skilled in the greedy, skilled in the non-greedy;
Free from greed and free from agitation, I bow down to that Buddha.
(678) Skilled in conceptual proliferation and skilled in the absence of proliferation, free from proliferation and without guile—I bow down to that Buddha. (679)
He awakened to all phenomena, the liberator from all evils;
having transcended all suffering, I bow down to that Buddha. 680.
He is wise regarding all things, having reached the further shore by abandoning evil.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the complete stilling of all conditioned phenomena.
681. I bow down to that Buddha who has expounded the Dharma of Truth, the destroyer of all evil, and who is liberated from the bases of evil. 682.
I bow down to that Buddha who, contemplating all phenomena, dried up all evil; who abandoned all craving;
and who, as a master of all things, released [beings] from the snare of evil.
Liberated from all acquisitions, I bow down to that Buddha. 684.
A Wheel-Turner, a King of Dhamma, adorned with the Wheel of Dhamma;
you crushed the wheel of unrighteousness—I bow down to that Buddha. 685.
I bow down to that Buddha who, having been anointed at the head of the True Dhamma,
the wise one, the great king of Dhamma, established the teaching of the Dhamma. He is the Lord of Dhamma,
the Master of Dhamma, the Sovereign of Dhamma, the Proclaimer of Dhamma.
Dhammasūro, the teacher of Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
(687) Dhammarañño, lord of Dhamma, master of Dhamma, sovereign of Dhamma;
Dhammabhūpo, ruler of Dhamma, overlord of Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. (688)
The great sovereign king of the Dhamma, honored by all as the Dhamma itself;
the one whose power is the Dhamma, the heir of the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow down.
He is the protection of the Dhamma, the refuge of the Dhamma, the giver of the shelter of the Dhamma.
To him who has Dhamma as his power, Dhamma as his abode—to that Buddha I bow down.
(690) To the giver of Dhamma, the father of Dhamma, the proclaimer of Dhamma, the friend of Dhamma;
to him whose happiness is Dhamma, who is devoted to Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow down. (691)
The elephant of the Dhamma, the lion of the Dhamma, the thoroughbred horse of the Dhamma, the bull of the Dhamma;
the wise one who bears the burden of the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow.
The horn of the Dhamma, the peak of the Dhamma, the Meru of the Dhamma, the mountain of the Dhamma.
Dhammakūṭa, Dhammasīsa—I bow down to that Buddha.
(693) Dhammādicca, Dhammappabha, Dibba, Dhammavibhākara;
Dhammabhākara, Dhammābha—I bow down to that Buddha. (694)
I bow down to that Buddha, the crest-jewel of the Dhamma, the pinnacle of the summit of the Dhamma, the beautiful crest-gem of the Dhamma.
Adorned with the ornaments of the Dhamma, embellished by the decorations of the Dhamma.
Adorned with the jewels of the Dhamma, I bow down to that Buddha.
(696) The island of the Dhamma, the radiance of the Dhamma, the light of the Dhamma, the splendor of the Dhamma;
the illuminator of the Dhamma, the sun of the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. (697)
Guarded by the Dhamma, freed from evil, yoked to the Dhamma, with the Dhamma as his abode;
known by the Dhamma, conscious of the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
Seeing the Dhamma, perceiving the Dhamma, beholding the Dhamma, he is possessed of true vision.
Dhammavipassī, Supassī—I bow down to that Buddha.
(699) Dhammadakkhī, Dhammasakkhī, Dhammarakkhī, Dhammadhara;
Saddhammapekkhī, Upekkhī—I bow down to that Buddha. (700)
One who perceives the Dhamma, one with wisdom in the Dhamma, one who has direct knowledge of the Dhamma, one who knows the Dhamma;
one who is blessed, one whose ultimate refuge is the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow.
One who knows the Dhamma, one who speaks the Dhamma, one who utters the Dhamma, one who is a knower of the Dhamma.
Speaking with measured words, speaking with honeyed sweetness—I bow down to that Buddha.
(702) Speaker of the Dhamma, perfected in the Dhamma; possessor of knowledge, ocean of knowledge;
possessor of wisdom, treasury of wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha. (703)
Guardian of the Dhamma, protector of the Dhamma; guardian of the Buddha, protector of enlightenment;
guardian of wisdom and guardian of intelligence—to that Buddha, I pay homage.
(704) Freed from what is not-Dhamma, one who shines with the Dhamma; freed from ignorance, one who shines with knowledge.
Freed from ignorance, possessing the light of true knowledge—to that Buddha I bow.
705. Ocean of the Dhamma, sea of the Dhamma, infinite ocean of the Dhamma;
mine of jewels of the True Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow. 706.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained inspired eloquence regarding the Dhamma,
who is an expert in the practice of the Dhamma, and who knows the Path of the Analytical Knowledges (Paṭisambhidāmagga).
Delighted and fully contented with the Dhamma, the wise one is firmly established in the Dhamma.
Established as the foremost, you are the foremost; I bow down to that Buddha.
(708) You have raised high the banner of liberation and lowered the banner of Māra;
you are the remover of evil and the remover of sorrow; I bow down to that Buddha. (709)
Having avoided all taints, having attained the Dhamma that leads to liberation, and being endowed with perfected virtues—I bow down to that Buddha. 710.
He poured forth the stream of Dhamma, the stopper of the streams of evil.
You gladdened those who were unsatisfied with the hearing [of the Dhamma]; I bow down to that Buddha.
(711) A cloud of Dhamma, a cloud of wisdom, you rained down the nectar of the Dhamma;
you washed away the dust and mire; I bow down to that Buddha. (712)
One whose nature is the Dhamma, the proclaimer of the Dhamma, the teacher of the path of the Dhamma;
you who have expounded the Dhamma in detail according to the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
Having known all knowable phenomena, you have thoroughly transcended the phenomena that are to be known.
Perfectly endowed with the knowledge of the higher powers, I bow down to that Buddha.
Having attained all the true Dhamma, having crossed the ocean of saṃsāra,
and being completely liberated from all evil, I bow down to that Buddha.
He whose nature is perfected, whose purpose is accomplished, who is honored by the entire cycle of existence, the most excellent of all, walking in perfect conduct—to that Buddha I bow. 716.
He who acts according to the Dhamma, who upholds the Dhamma, who lives by the Dhamma, and who is devoted to the Dhamma.
Essence of the Dhamma, embodiment of the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
Eldest of the Dhamma, best of the Dhamma, pure in the Dhamma, stainless in the Dhamma;
banner of the Dhamma, standard of the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
I bow down to that Buddha who loves the Dhamma, who has become the Dhamma, who delights in the Dhamma, who is a sage,
who is devoted to the Dhamma, and who is free from passion. (719) He who knows the Dhamma,
the dispeller of evil, who dwells in the Dhamma, and who is righteous in the Dhamma.
He has shown the Deathless Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha.
(720) The body of Dhamma, the form of Dhamma, named Dhamma, joyful in Dhamma;
established in Dhamma, established in liberation—I bow down to that Buddha. (721)
I bow to that Buddha, the bearer of the Dhamma, the steadfast one, who is like the full moon filled with the Dhamma; he has reached the depths of the Deathless.
He is the skilled physician of the Dhamma, the remover of the arrow, the extractor of the dart.
To that Buddha, the great benefactor, the physician, I bow down.
723. To that Buddha, the Sakka of Dhamma, perfected in Dhamma, resplendent with the crown of Dhamma, beloved of Dhamma, peaceful in Dhamma, I bow down. 724.
To the knower of the Dhamma, the speaker of the Dhamma, the giver of the Dhamma, the bestower of the Path;
to the one who has mastered the Dhamma, the source of the Dhamma—to that Buddha, I pay homage.
He made known the Deathless Dhamma and brought many people across to safety.
To the physician for those who are afflicted, that Buddha I bow down.
Sharing in the Dhamma, abandoning evil, partaking of the Dhamma, having cast off evil;
delighting in the Dhamma, rejoicing in the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow down.
To him who knows the Dhamma, who has realized the Dhamma, who sees the Dhamma, who is devoted to the Dhamma;
to him who lives according to the Dhamma, who is proficient in the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow.
To the bearer of the Dhamma and its conformity to the Dhamma, who removes the burning heat of those [afflictions].
I bow down to that Buddha, the breaker of fear and its opposite.
(729) I bow down to that Buddha, the bearer of the pure Dhamma, the benefactor in every way, who walks with beautiful conduct. (730)
I bow down to that Buddha, who drinks from the nectar of the Dhamma, whose heart is gentle like a honey-bee, and who churns out the pure essence of the True Dhamma.
He is the giver of the Dhamma that is verifiable by one's own experience, directly visible, and timeless.
Leading to liberation, well-expounded—I bow down to that Buddha.
(732) Drinking the nectar of the pure Dhamma, you enjoyed the fruit of liberation;
eating peace, consuming happiness—I bow down to that Buddha. (733)
Honored, possessing majesty, of great psychic power, and highly revered;
the sovereign of the Great True Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow. 734.
He who instructs others by taking himself as his own refuge, the wise one who is the instructor;
He who instructed [me] by taking refuge in the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
(735) Having cultivated and frequently practiced the factors conducive to enlightenment, he attained perfect self-enlightenment—I bow down to that Buddha. (736)
Wise, endowed with steadfastness, the best of the resolute, a follower of the true Dhamma;
joined with the foundation of the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in the inclination toward the Dhamma, free from doubt regarding all phenomena.
Having reached the ultimate goal, I bow down to that Buddha.
(738) Strong in fortitude, upholder of fortitude, bearer of fortitude, crest-jewel of wisdom;
the wise one who seeks the supreme Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. (739)
He has dispelled all torment, he is the dispeller of all evil;
having attained the fruit of all qualities, I bow down to that Buddha.
740. He is detached from all evils, liberated from all unwholesome states.
I bow down to that Buddha who brings an end to all suffering.
(741) I bow down to that Buddha who is liberated from evil in every way, established in the pure Dhamma, and who has released [beings] from all suffering. (742)
I bow down to that Buddha who has abandoned all evil, who has reached the further shore of all phenomena, and who has crossed over the flood of terrible suffering.
He has shattered every unwholesome state and brought about the destruction of all evil.
He who cuts all bonds—I bow down to that Buddha.
(744) He who protects against all superhuman states, who dispels all evil, and who has extinguished all suffering—I bow down to that Buddha. (745)
The liberator from suffering, the giver of liberation, the capable leader of the caravan;
the destroyer of evil, the speaker of the Dhamma—to that Buddha I bow. 746.
The sharer of the Dhamma, the abandoner of evil, the abandoner of passion, the sharer of generosity.
I bow down to that Buddha who partakes of happiness and abandons suffering.
(747) I bow down to that Buddha who lives rightly, who lives by the Dhamma, who lives a pure life, who lives a clean life, who lives by virtue, and who lives by truth. (748)
Living by wisdom, living by what is known, living by knowledge, living by the supreme;
living by true science, living by discernment—to that Buddha I bow.
Living by patience, living by peace, living by uprightness, living by rectitude.
Living on joy, feeding on joy—I bow down to that Buddha.
Living on the divine, living on the capable, living on the auspicious, living on equanimity;
living on gladness, living on loving-kindness—I bow down to that Buddha.
One who lives by the gut, one who lives by pearls, one who lives by ivory, one who lives by restraint;
one who lives by skill, one who lives by excellence—to that Buddha I bow. One who lives for the welfare of others, one who lives for happiness, one who lives by meditation, one who lives by vows.
He who lives on the nectar [of the Dhamma], who lives in purity—I bow down to that Buddha.
(753) He who lives with a purified life, who is thoroughly cleansed; he who lives in contentment, who is well-satisfied;
he who lives a preeminent life, who is exalted—I bow down to that Buddha. (754)
Bearing loving-kindness, practicing loving-kindness, acting with loving-kindness, abiding in loving-kindness;
having loving-kindness as his home, having loving-kindness as his essence—I bow down to that Buddha.
755. Bearing peace, creating peace, practicing peace, peaceful in mind;
Peaceful in essence, peaceful in mind—to that Buddha I bow.
Bearing patience, practicing patience, walking in patience, with a mind of patience;
joined with patience, having patience as one's essence—to that Buddha I bow.
One who creates happiness, one who moves in happiness, one who maintains happiness, one who brings happiness;

one whose essence is happiness, one whose mind is happiness—to that Buddha I bow. 758. One who acts for the welfare of others, one who maintains welfare, one who moves toward welfare, one who brings about welfare;
I bow down to that Buddha, who acts for the welfare of others and seeks their well-being.

759. I bow down to that Buddha, who conducts himself with wisdom, whose essence is wisdom, who possesses wisdom, who is the abode of wisdom, who is the sun of wisdom, and who is the light of wisdom. 760.
Possessing wisdom, moving with wisdom, upholding wisdom, the abode of wisdom;
the moon of wisdom, the lord of wisdom—to that Buddha I bow down. 761.
He who creates loving-kindness, he who creates joy, the skillful one, the creator of welfare.
Wise in conduct, the maker of wisdom—to that Buddha I bow.
Light-maker, sky-maker, compassionate, the maker of compassion;
fearless, the maker of fearlessness—to that Buddha I bow.
The maker of security, the maker of beauty, the maker of happiness, the maker of welfare;
the remover of spears, the remover of stakes—to that Buddha I bow down. 764.
The maker of great safety, the one who is secure, the maker of great wisdom, the Lord.
I bow down to that Buddha, the peaceful one who brings great peace. 765.
I bow down to that Buddha, the protector of the protectorless, the granter of fearlessness to those who are afraid, and the provider of refuge to the wretched. 766.
Far-seeing, long-seeing, seeing the end, having reached the further shore;
seeing the bank, seeing the beyond—to that Buddha I bow.
Seeing the essence, seeing the truth, seeing the auspicious, beautiful to behold.
To the Seer of Yoga, the Seer of Security, that Buddha I bow down.
To the Seer of Peace, the Seer of Happiness, the Seer of Purity, the Pure-minded One;
To the Foremost Seer, the Seer of the Permanent, that Buddha I bow down.
I bow to that Buddha who sees the supramundane Dhamma, the seer who perceives the ultimate limit, the seer of the Path, and the seer of the Fruits. 770.
He is the Seer of Meaning, the Seer of the Way, the Peerless Seer, and the Beautiful Seer.
Seeing the supreme, seeing well, I bow down to that Buddha. 771.
Seeing destruction, seeing passing away, seeing the way, beautiful to behold;
seeing the inexhaustible, seeing clearly, I bow down to that Buddha. 772.
To the one who sees the deathless, the direct witness, the observer, the purifier;
to the one who has attained the analytical knowledges—to that Buddha I bow.
773. All-pervading, all-seeing, all-observer, all-knowing;
He has fully understood everything; I bow down to that Buddha.
(774) Having destroyed craving for sensual existence and crushing craving for non-existence, he has pulverized all craving; I bow down to that Buddha. (775)
The destruction of the fetter of craving, the crushing of the thorn of craving—craving has been eradicated by him; I bow down to that Buddha. 776.
Craving for sensual pleasures is utterly exhausted, and he has transcended craving for existence.
I bow down to that Buddha who has destroyed the craving for existence.
777. I bow down to that Buddha who brings contentment to those seeking joy, who satisfies those who are weary, and who, having transcended craving, is forever satisfied. 778.
I bow down to that Buddha who destroys the net of defilements,
washes away the stain of craving, and dries up the stream of saṃsāra—
779. Who has relinquished all acquisitions and shattered the web of craving.
You have pierced through the hindrances; I bow down to that Buddha.
780. With the cave of the heart utterly exhausted, with craving and its support abandoned, and with the underlying tendency of ignorance severed—I bow down to that Buddha. 781.
Having struck down the dart of craving, the possessor of the three knowledges who has abandoned death and attained supreme enlightenment—I bow to that Buddha. 782.
You have disentangled the tangle of craving, driving out all traces of attachment in every respect.
You destroyed the passion for delight; I bow down to that Buddha. 783.
Having transcended all cravings, you dried up the stream of thirst;
you set flowing the stream of Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha. 784.
I bow down to that Buddha who has reached the destruction of all craving, who has dispelled all suffering, and who has incinerated all acquisitions.
He has suppressed all cravings and is one whose every desire has been stilled.
He completely cut off all sensations; I bow down to that Buddha. 786.
The ascetic shattered all sensations, having transcended all craving;
he abandoned all desires; I bow down to that Buddha. 787.
Having crossed the ocean of craving, having abandoned all that is wrong and undesirable, you have released the arrow of the mind; I bow down to that Buddha.
You have avoided the cycle of karma; you are free from the defilements of action.
Restrained in every way, a hero—I bow down to that Buddha.
789. Unattached, perfectly tranquil, having transcended desire, anger, and fear;
skillful in abandoning existence and karma—I bow down to that Buddha. 790.
A lion free from timidity, with fear and dread cut away,
who has attained the destruction of existence and karma— to that Buddha I bow.
He has incinerated the seeds of karma, having scraped away the root of delusion.
I bow down to that Buddha who has eradicated underlying tendencies. 792.
I bow down to that Buddha who has completely exhausted all karma, who has eliminated all karmic results, and who has abandoned all merit and demerit. 793.
He has carried away all karma and all defilements without remainder;
he has liberated me from every knot—to that Buddha I bow. 794.
He is liberated from all karmas, having completely renounced all karma.
Endowed with all the qualities of desire, I bow down to that Buddha.
795. You shattered the root of ignorance, you destroyed the machinery of karma;
having attained the destruction of all karma, I bow down to that Buddha. 796.
Having crushed the doctrine of non-existence, he established the doctrine of existence;
he made known right view—to that Buddha I bow. 797. The Protector, who has washed away internal defilements and crossed to the further shore of the flood of the three realms of existence;
Subhaga, pure in every way—to that Buddha I bow.
Best of elephants, best of lions, caravan leader, best of teachers;
ocean of wisdom, bearer of the steadfast—to that Buddha I bow.
Dispeller of heat, dispeller of suffering, giver of all welfare and happiness, with lovely speech and dear speech—to that Buddha I bow down. 800.
Endowed with conduct, possessing the threefold knowledge, having utterly uprooted [the defilements] by cutting them at the root.
Having attained his final birth, I bow down to that Buddha. 801.
A wonder to the three realms of existence, an extraordinary banner of the three worlds, the most excellent flag of the True Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha. 802.
With senses restrained, with senses at peace, with the faculty of serene confidence, with well-cultivated faculties—tranquil, I bow down to that Buddha. 803.
Endowed with wisdom like the earth, joined with fortitude like a mountain;
Endowed with patience, equal to the earth—homage to that Buddha. 804.
Possessing immeasurable glory, adorned with the ornament of peace, graced with the jewelry of happiness—homage to that Buddha. 805.
I bow down to that Buddha who has accumulated the thirty perfections, crossed over the ocean of the three realms of existence,
and is joined with his final birth. He has fully understood the taints of becoming,
and he is the pacifier of the exhaustion of all evil.
Having attained supreme bliss, I bow down to that Buddha.

(807) One who has reached what is auspicious, who proclaims what is auspicious, who reveals the auspicious path, whose vision is auspicious, and who sees what is auspicious—I bow down to that Buddha. (808)
To him of great psychic power and wisdom,
who has reached the end of existence-to-existence and attained the fruit of the Deathless— to that Buddha I bow down.
(809) The Blessed One partakes of Nibbāna, has attained peace, and possesses sublime fortune.
Having attained supreme peace, I bow down to that Buddha.
(810) Endowed with the virtues of right conduct, a mine of all qualities, as full as the full moon, I bow down to that Buddha. (811)
With delight and passion utterly destroyed, liberated from grasping, the supreme among men, the seeker of security—him, the Buddha, I bow down to. 812.
He who performs what is to be done, whose task is accomplished, and who reveals what should and should not be done.
Skilled in the settlement of legal matters, I bow down to that Buddha.
(813) The supreme sage who is perfectly tranquil, the preeminent sage who is proficient, the most excellent bull among seers—I bow down to that Buddha. (814)
I bow down to that Buddha who has abandoned fear and terror, who is confident amidst assemblies, and who roars the lion’s roar of a man. 815.
He who goes to the further shore and has reached the further shore, the preeminent one who has gone to the limit.
The Knower of the World, who has reached the end of the world—to that Buddha I bow.
816. Perfect in the ultimate meaning, seeing the supreme truth, he who has realized Nibbāna—to that Buddha I bow. 817.
In gain and loss, in fame and disgrace, in honor and dishonor—he who is equal in all respects, that Lord, the Buddha, I bow down to. 818.
The Wise One has attained the ultimate goal; he is supremely pure and most excellent.
I bow down to that Buddha who has liberated one from the bond of existence.
819. I bow down to that Buddha who is worthy, fully awakened, the liberator from saṃsāra, and endowed with perfect tranquility. 820.
Through the full understanding of the five aggregates, and being perfected by wisdom, he crushed all delusion—I bow down to that Buddha. 821.
A supreme man, striving, seeking the further shore, he has reached the further shore.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained seclusion. 822.
I bow down to that Buddha who has reached the destruction of all defilements, who has shaken off all underlying tendencies, and who has abandoned all taints. 823.
He completely severed all ignorance, bearing the sharp weapon of wisdom;
he destroyed every latent tendency—to that Buddha I bow. 824.
He has transcended all sorrow, the destroyer of all suffering.
I bow down to that Buddha who has utterly severed all distress. 825.
He proclaimed the path to liberation, seeking the path to liberation himself;
freed from the disease of all existence, I bow down to that Buddha. 826.
He who is not smeared by sensual desires, like a mustard seed on the tip of an awl, and is liberated from the fetter of existence—to that Buddha I bow. 827.
The Sage, perfected in sagehood, the Brahmin who has cast out evil.
The ascetic who has attained equanimity— to that Buddha I bow.
The taint of existence has been shaken off, the taint of sensual desire has been stilled,
and the taint of ignorance has vanished— to that Buddha I bow.
To him who has fully understood what is to be understood, developed what is to be developed, and abandoned what is to be abandoned—to that Buddha I bow. 830.
He has attained the bliss of peace and is the one who carries forth the stream of liberation.
You have liberated many beings—I bow down to that Buddha. 831.

You have reached the further shore of full understanding, you are the master who has reached the further shore of abandonment, and you are the powerful one who has reached the further shore of cultivation—I bow down to that Buddha. 832.
Free from the fault of attachment, liberated and without substrate;
released from bondage and cleansed—I bow down to that Buddha. 833.
Attained to Nibbāna, Siddhattha, free from impudence and having abandoned proliferation.
Awakened and having found refuge, I bow down to that Buddha.

(834) Established in the path and established in the fruit, the one who has rent asunder the net of delusion, the one who is well-composed and possesses perfect liberation—I bow down to that Buddha. (835)
Endowed with the jewel of enlightenment, possessed of excellent and vast wisdom—the Brahmin, the ascetic, the virtuous one—I bow down to that Buddha. 836.
You have pulverized wrong view and crushed wrong conduct.
He warded off wrong knowledge; I bow down to that Buddha.
(837) Having transcended the net of delusion, he was the ender of the wicked and the destroyer of the end;
he crushed the intoxication of Māra; I bow down to that Buddha. (838)
Siddhattha, who has attained his own goal, whose every aspiration is fulfilled, who has done what was to be done and is utterly tranquil—to that Buddha I bow. 839.
He from whom illusion, conceit, delusion, and hypocrisy have been cast down;
Like water on a lotus leaf, I bow down to that Buddha. 840.
Stainless like the king of stars, pure-minded and untroubled;
unattached, the Well-Gone One, the Protector—I bow down to that Buddha. 841.
Having completely exhausted existence in the realm of desire and transcended existence in the realm of form, you shattered existence in the formless realm—I bow down to that Buddha. 842.
Renowned and adorned with glory, a great sage, an elephant among seers;
Hitesī, the source of welfare—I bow down to that Buddha. 843.
Tapassī, Tejassī, Yasassī, and Yasodhara;
Vipassī and Vidassī—I bow down to that Buddha. 844.
Seeker of the supreme path, bringer of happiness to all living beings, Great Sage, Great Seer—I bow down to that Buddha. 845.
Knower of the meaning, knower of truth, knower of the world, one who has reached the end of the world;
A traveler who has gone the journey’s end—I bow down to that Buddha. 846.
Shattered by the thorn of the arrow of sorrow, having incinerated all grasping, the Hero who has crossed the swamp of delusion—I bow down to that Buddha. 847.
Having transcended fear and terror, fearless and free from trepidation, liberated in every way from trembling—to that Buddha I bow. 848.
The Protector, delighting in the unproliferated (nippapañca), has demonstrated the unproliferated.
He has caused all conceptual proliferation to cease; I bow down to that Buddha.
849. The advisor, the enlightener, the savior of many beings, the Teacher skilled in exposition—I bow down to that Buddha. 850.
Pure-hearted and thoroughly cleansed, stainless with a dust-free mind,
a bathed one with a spotless heart— to that Buddha I bow.
One for whom the cycle of birth has been exhausted, bearing his final body.
Not wandering in saṃsāra, I bow down to that Buddha.
(852) At the feet of Dīpaṅkara, you renounced liberation already within your grasp;
desiring perfect enlightenment, I bow down to that Buddha. (853)
Speaking kindly, speaking with love, one who speaks kindly and is clothed in speech;
one whose speech is lovely, whose speech is charming—to that Buddha I bow down. 854.
One whose speech is firm, whose speech is secure, whose speech is joyful, who proclaims peace.
Speaking clearly, speaking precisely—I bow down to that Buddha. (855) Speaking with wisdom, knowing wisdom;
speaking at the right time, knowing the right time;
speaking the truth, knowing the truth—I bow down to that Buddha. (856)
I bow to that Buddha who speaks with the voice of a karavīka bird,

who possesses wisdom, who teaches the profound Dhamma, who is a versatile and wonderful speaker of varied discourses. He is fully endowed with perfect enlightenment and is resplendent with the power of the True Dhamma.
To him who has perfected both knowledge and conduct, to that Buddha I bow.
(858) In whom no taints exist, whose mind is forever liberated, who has attained the supreme state—to that Buddha I bow. (859)
The ascetic who has attained tranquility, the brahmin who dwells in the sublime abodes—he has cast off every stain;
I bow down to that Buddha. 860. He whose craving for existence is utterly exhausted, who has crossed over the flood of becoming, delusion, and death;
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the state of supreme excellence.
861. I bow down to that Buddha who has transcended the five hindrances, who maintains the seven purifications, and who is skilled in the seven factors of enlightenment. 862.
Having fulfilled all the perfections, seeking only the pure Dhamma, he proclaimed the path to liberation; I pay homage to that Buddha. 863.
He who overcame the world, who conquered the world, who knows the world, the leader of the world;
The Lord of the Three Worlds, the Sovereign of the World—to that Buddha I bow.
(864) Named Subhatthin, of noble name, whose name is truth and who brings happiness;
true to his bond and truthful in speech—to that Buddha I bow. (865)
Having abandoned sensual lust, free from the sense of "mine," and without a home;
unattached, well-gone, and pure—to that Buddha I bow. 866. One who has reached the fulfillment of what was to be fulfilled, and who is perfected in the power of direct knowledge.
I bow to that Buddha who has reached the destruction of birth and death.
867. I bow to that Buddha who has utterly severed illusion and delusion, who has torn asunder the flow of hatred, and who has dispelled the craving for greed. 868.
With the arrows of the defilements completely severed, his mind unattached, firm-minded and free from anguish—to that Buddha I bow. 869.
The Teacher, whose mind is fully blossomed, is always possessed of a serene heart.
With a joyful mind, O Lord, I bow down to that Buddha. 870.
With a stainless mind, O Protector, always with a pure mind;
with a purified mind, being pure—O Buddha, I bow down to you. 871.
Radiant and rich in radiance, ascetic and rich in asceticism, seeker of knowledge and rich in knowledge—to that Buddha I bow. 872.
Delighted, you caused delight; bringing satisfaction, you satisfied others.
The Protector protected him; I bow down to that Buddha.
(873) Having brought his vows to completion, perfected in the power of direct knowledge, he reached the destruction of birth and death; I bow down to that Buddha. (874)
I bow down to that Buddha who has utterly eradicated illusion and delusion, who has torn asunder the flow of hatred, and who has dispelled the craving of greed. 875.
He has completely uprooted the arrow of hatred, and his mind is unattached.
Firm-minded and free from distress—to that Buddha I bow. 876.
He made known the Dhamma together with its cause; the ardent, meditative brahmin dispelled all doubts—to that Buddha I bow. 877.
The Brahmin, ardent and meditative, has sown away all doubts;
knowing the exhaustion of conditions, I bow down to that Buddha.
Having defeated the army of Māra, you shine like the sun.
Having attained the true Dhamma, I bow down to that Buddha.
(879) He fulfilled the thirty perfections, bringing benefit to the entire world;
he sought the Four Noble Truths—I bow down to that Buddha. (880)
Having realized the Four Noble Truths, he attained the destruction of craving;
with a mind that has reached the unconditioned, I bow down to that Buddha.
881. Of auspicious body, auspicious speech, auspicious mind, and auspicious disposition;
Samantabhadra, the truly auspicious—him I bow to as the Buddha.
(882) With body calmed, speech calmed, and mind calmed, you have reached the ocean of peace; him I bow to as the Buddha. (883)
Friend of the world, Lord of the world, Sovereign of the world, Master of the world;
Friend of the world, Companion of the world—to that Buddha I bow.
(884) He who has reached the further shore of the combination of letters, both preceding and succeeding;
Skilled in the words of etymological analysis, to that Buddha I bow.
885. Bestower of the state of peace and happiness, treasure-house of knowledge, leader, helper to many people, to that Buddha I bow. 886.
Victorious at the foot of the Bodhi tree, having attained supreme enlightenment, the end-maker of the end-maker—I bow down to that Buddha. 887.
He who speaks the Discipline is dispassionate; he who speaks the Dhamma has entered the Dhamma.
I bow down to that Buddha who speaks of the goal and has attained the goal. 888.
I bow down to that Buddha who speaks of peace, who speaks with gentleness, who speaks the truth and delights in truth, who speaks what is real and speaks auspiciously. 889.
Restrained in body, restrained in speech, restrained in mind, and restrained in the senses—the ascetic who is thus restrained in every way, that Buddha I revere. 890.
Without desire, with desire severed, beyond desire, with craving cut off;
I bow down to that Buddha who has transcended both desire and aversion regarding the realms of existence.
891. I bow down to that Buddha whose mind is pure, whose conduct is pure, who does not pursue impure desires, and who has utterly severed all longing and lack of longing. 892.
Blazing with the fire of wisdom, the highest of the blazing, the supreme among the blazing;
having attained the deathless, the unconditioned—I bow down to that Buddha. 893.
Pure, he purified the Path; perfected, the crest-jewel of recluses.
The Buddha proclaimed enlightenment; I bow down to that Buddha.
Exquisite, pure, holy, and purifying;
gracious, supreme, and most excellent—I bow down to that Buddha.
Secure, with fever extinguished, yoked to security, the maker of security;

a field of security, a place of security—to that Buddha I bow. 896. One whose enjoyments have passed away, one whose diseases have passed away, one whose sorrow has passed away, one who is free from turbidity;
Free from regret, free from attachment—to that Buddha I bow.
One who has gone beyond all sufferings, one who has reached the further shore through full understanding;
to that Buddha, by whom cessation has been well realized, I bow.
Endowed with the seven purifications, pure and with a purified mind,
wise and with a liberated mind— to that Buddha I bow.
Having experienced existence after existence, he has attained the supreme, ultimate liberation.
He set in motion the Wheel of Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha.
(900) Possessing vast wisdom, possessing vast intellect, he was the proclaimer of vast enlightenment;
he extended his vast knowledge; I bow down to that Buddha. (901)
The Hero who laid down the burden, who destroyed the craving for existence, and who dismantled the conduit to becoming—to that Buddha I bow. 902.
He whose self was cultivated, liberated from existence, developed, and delighting in cultivation;
The Blessed One has cultivated his faculties; I bow down to that Buddha.
(903) The Great Physician, the medicine, the healer of the disease of existence;
the auspicious one who carries one across the flood of existence—I bow down to that Buddha. (904)
Broken by craving for existence and non-existence, he shattered the attachment to becoming;
he severed the fetter of becoming—to that Buddha I bow. 905.
Subhadda, seeing the end of becoming, has transcended the peak of existence and attained Nibbāna.
The Blessed Ones have gone to the end of existence; I bow down to that Buddha.
(906) The Noble Path has been cultivated, leading to the complete destruction of the bonds of existence;
he shattered all fear and terror—I bow down to that Buddha. (907)
You cultivate wholesome states, possessing the jewel of the factors of enlightenment;
the Protector has crossed the stream of existence—to that Buddha I bow. 908.
Having severed the fetter of existence, the Seer has transcended the attachment to existence.
Having crossed over the ocean of existence, I bow down to that Buddha. 909.

Having transcended the bonds of existence, having been cooled by the extinction of the fever of existence, and having crossed the ocean of delusion regarding existence, I bow down to that Buddha. 910.
Detached from the defilements of existence and enjoyment, released from the burden, the conqueror of existence;
liberated from the fetters of existence—to that Buddha I bow. 911.
Having crossed over the flood of existence and enjoyment, he is the burner of the net of existence.
Having transcended the wandering of existence, I bow down to that Buddha. 912.
A refuge for the fearful, a leader for the fearful, a giver of safety to the fearful, and a protector of the fearful even more— I bow down to that Buddha. 913.
The refuge for all who seek refuge, the protection, the shelter, the excellent guardian;
the one who brings exceeding joy to people—to that Buddha I bow down.
He has transcended all afflictions and brought an end to the darkness of craving.
I bow down to that Buddha who abandoned the taint of sensual desire. 915.
I bow down to that Buddha who has fully awakened to all phenomena, who sought the path to liberation, and who has attained the ultimate truth of the Dhamma. 916.
The Victor, who brings an end to the thorns of existence, has awakened to all phenomena;
having reached the limit of all things, I bow down to that Buddha. 917.
He has fully understood the entire world and is the one who has cast off the whole world.
Having attained the supramundane Dhamma, I bow down to that Buddha. 918.
For the sake of the welfare and benefit of the entire world, you awakened through the mastery of compassion;
having attained the Dhamma of subtle meaning, I bow down to that Buddha. 919.
He has directly known all powers, he is the extinguisher of all craving;
he has realized cessation—him, the Buddha, I pay homage. 920.
He has directly known all truths, the All-Knowing One, the Supreme Ascetic.
Wise in all phenomena, I bow down to that Buddha.
(921) Having accomplished all goals, auspicious in every way, and having attained the most excellent Dhamma, I bow down to that Buddha. (922)
Endowed with the qualities of enlightenment, liberated from all states of existence, having attained what is desired and being freed from the undesired—I bow down to that Buddha. 923.
Having fully understood all nutriment, he is independent of all nutriment.
I bow down to that Buddha who has relinquished all supports.
Having destroyed all delusion and dispelled all lust and hatred, he proclaimed the Dhamma of purity; I bow down to that Buddha.
He dried up all defilements, he drove away all obstacles;
he destroyed all sorrow—I bow down to that Buddha. 926.
He is the Master who guards all his faculties, restrained from all doubt and craving.
I bow down to that Buddha who has renounced all worldly desires;
927. I bow down to that Buddha who has abandoned all taints and warded off birth and death; he shattered the suffering of existence. 928.
I bow down to that Buddha who has abandoned all karma and defilements, whose mind is free from volitional formations, and who has attained his final body.
He has severed every bond and is the destroyer of all obstacles.
Knowing the path to enlightenment and liberated from dull-wittedness—I bow down to that Buddha. 930.
With all delusion utterly destroyed, omniscient and skilled in all things;
the conqueror of all, the knower of all—I bow down to that Buddha. 931.
Empty of all dogmatic attachments, established in all virtues,
he purified himself of all defilements— I bow down to that Buddha.
He shone forth, free from all lust, the destroyer of all hatred.
Completely liberated from all delusion, I bow down to that Buddha. 933.
Having fully understood all suffering and bringing about the destruction of all suffering, the shatterer of existence in every way—I bow down to that Buddha. 934.
Having transcended all suffering, having gone to the end of all suffering, and having abandoned all suffering—to that Buddha I bow down. 935.
Having crossed the ocean of saṃsāra, he has reached the further shore of all states of existence.
You have borne your final body; I bow down to that Buddha.
936. Transcending all desires, wise and having gone beyond all attachments, unstained by anything; I bow down to that Buddha. 937.
I bow down to that Buddha who has abandoned restlessness, who has destroyed craving,
who stands firm in all forms of relinquishment, and who is completely tranquil in every respect.
Having brought all enemies under his control, he is the Conqueror of All, the Overcomer of All.
Completely liberated from all enemies, I bow down to that Buddha.
Having transcended all enjoyments, having abandoned all delight in sensual pleasures,
with all doubt and craving cut off, I bow down to that Buddha.
Having transcended all fears, the destroyer of all terrors;
the subduer of all faults and cravings—to that Buddha I bow. 941.
He in whom all agitation and anger have perished, who has transcended desire and the afflictions.
Freed from all delusion and illusion, I bow down to that Buddha.
(942) Having severed all fetters, having gone beyond all doubt, and having cut off all clinging, I bow down to that Buddha. (943)
He has caused all desires to fall away, he is the purifier of all defilements, and all his cravings have been stilled—to that Buddha I bow. 944.
He is the relinquisher of all gifts, he has transcended all fetters.
Detached from all attachments, to that Buddha I bow. 945.
The Lord is well-disposed toward all, the bestower of universal well-being;
he brings serene confidence to all—to that Buddha I bow. 946.
He extinguished every fire, the crusher of all feverish distress;
being liberated in every respect and peaceful, I bow down to that Buddha.
He fully understood all taints, the destroyer of all diseases.
I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the destruction of all sorrow. 948.
I bow down to that Buddha who has dispelled the darkness of all passion, who has driven away the darkness of all hatred, and who has destroyed the darkness of all delusion. 949.
The Seer who has attained all things in every way, who sees everything everywhere—he crushed all sectarian doctrines; to that Buddha I bow. 950.
He who is born of all perfections, fulfilled by the full comprehension of all things.
Perfectly endowed with all super-knowledges, I bow down to that Buddha.
(951) Having attained the destruction of all suffering, having transcended all sorrow, and having crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra, I bow down to that Buddha. (952)
Endowed with virtue and concentration, possessing the ocean of true knowledge and wisdom, having severed and shattered all taints—to that Buddha I bow. 953.
Completely liberated from all feverish distress, with all acquisitions utterly destroyed;
The stilling of all conceptual proliferation—to that Buddha I bow.
954. Freed from all "I-making," with the destruction of all "mine-making," and utterly released from all attachment—to that Buddha I bow. 955.
Having conquered all battles, undefeated in every respect,
you have brought all under your sway in every way— to that Buddha I bow. All-knowing,
the best in the three worlds, the remover of all fetters.
You have crossed over all floods; I bow down to that Buddha.
(957) Released from all bonds, having cut through all knots, you have liberated [beings] from all snares; I bow down to that Buddha. (958)
With all fetters utterly severed, detached from all bonds, with agitation destroyed and the substrate eliminated—to that Buddha I bow. 959.
Empty of all fetters, the destroyer of all cyclic existence.
You untangled every tangle; I bow down to that Buddha.
(960) Perceiving non-desire toward all things, the seer who has transcended all covetousness and is unbound by all fetters—I bow down to that Buddha. (961)
Empty of all conditioned phenomena, having cast off all attachment, and liberated from all that is unwholesome—to that Buddha I bow. 962.
Endowed with every excellence, supremely auspicious in every way.
Perfect in every aspect, to that Buddha I bow.
Having attained all branches of knowledge,
the gatherer of all excellent virtues, auspicious and the doer of what is most good— to that Buddha I bow.
Having fully understood all taints, having brought all taints to an end, you have relinquished everything—I bow down to that Buddha. 965.
Completely liberated from all bonds, fulfilled in all noble intentions;
He has blossomed the safety from all [fear]; I bow down to that Buddha. 966.
The Teacher is skilled in all things, wise and learned in all things;
stainless and pure in all things—I bow down to that Buddha. 967.
Exalted in every way, auspicious in every respect, abandoning all conceit, endowed with perfect vision—to that Buddha I bow. 968.
Knower of knowledge without remainder, easily understood from every side.
All-encompassing knowledge has been severed; I bow down to that Buddha.
(969) The Protector has attained omniscience; he is detached from everything in every way;
he is the most distinguished in all respects; I bow down to that Buddha. (970)
Empty of all defilements, the liberator from all bonds, he who severed every fetter—to that Buddha I bow. 971.
All states of existence have been cut off; the ties to the world have been severed.
Having crossed over all floods, I bow down to that Buddha. 972.
Having crossed the ocean of existence, having accomplished what was to be done, the Lord of Ascetics, who has become entirely cooled—I bow down to that Buddha. 973.
The Sage who has overcome the entire world, who knows the entire world, who clearly beholds the entire world—to that Buddha I bow down. 974.
He who is detached from the entire world, who causes the entire world to be free from passion;
You have brought all the world to cessation; I bow down to that Buddha. 975.
Free from longing for the whole world, unattached to the whole world, empty of craving for the whole world—I bow down to that Buddha. 976.
Having attained all supernormal knowledges, the most excellent one of sublime wisdom has expounded every truth; I bow down to that Buddha.
977. Perfected in all perfections, having reached all virtues;
Having attained complete thorough knowledge of all things, I bow down to that Buddha.
978. You have diverted the stream of existence and transcended all defilements;
you have washed away all taints—I bow down to that Buddha. 979.
He has completely relinquished everything, both internal and external;
having realized all security, I bow down to that Buddha.
980. He who has abandoned all conceptual proliferation and stands firm in renunciation—
He has avoided all attachment; I bow down to that Buddha.
(981) All obstacles have been destroyed by him; he is extinguished by the fire of all evils;
he has shattered all aggression; I bow down to that Buddha. (982)
All longing has been severed, all conceit destroyed;
having relinquished all underlying tendencies, I bow down to that Buddha.
All social attachments have been cut off, and all fetters have been abandoned.
I bow down to that Buddha who has destroyed all odors [of defilement]. 984.
I bow down to that Buddha who has brought about the pacification of all clinging, who has shattered all doubts, and who has crushed every thorn [of suffering]. 985.
He dispelled all delusion, the crusher of all conceit;
having transcended all fear, I bow down to that Buddha. 986.
He brought the attachment to sensual desires to an end, the severer of all craving.
You have cut off all desires; I bow down to that Buddha.
(987) You have crushed all delusion, you who dry up the poison of all [wrong] views;
you have burnt away all knots; I bow down to that Buddha. (988)
He has transcended everything, he has abandoned all agitation;
having destroyed the stain of every fault, I bow down to that Buddha. 989.
He has overcome all anger, he is the crusher of all sensual desires.
I bow down to that Buddha who has utterly eradicated all delusion. 990.
You have completely severed the conduit to existence and are disgusted by all enjoyments;
endowed with all the qualities of enlightenment, I bow down to that Buddha. 991.
I bow down to that Buddha who has transcended all longing,
who has surpassed all conceit, and who is completely liberated from all faults.
He is freed from all doubt and has fallen away from all fetters.
Having crossed the entire flood of saṃsāra, I bow to that Buddha. 993.
Unstained by anything, all-knowing, and the conqueror of all;
with all obstacles exhausted, I bow to that Buddha. 994.
Having transcended all acquisitions, having brought about the destruction of all taints, like a lion without fear—to that Buddha I bow. 995.
Freed from all notions of "mine," with the destruction of all conceit of "I."
Having transcended all faults, I bow down to that Buddha.
996. Wearied by the path of all existence, extinguished through the cessation of all conditioned formations, he shattered all bonds; I bow down to that Buddha. 997.
You have eradicated all afflictions, you have relinquished all fetters, and you have renounced all cravings—
to that Buddha I bow down. You have abandoned all greed and the objects of greed,
and you have dispelled all delusion and deceit.
He has dispelled all covetousness—I bow down to that Buddha. 999.
He has transcended all resentment and anger, abandoned all hatred and defilements, and gone beyond all malice—I bow down to that Buddha. 1000.
He has become free from all passion, the destroyer of all hatred,
and has transcended all delusion— to that Buddha I bow.
He has washed away every stain and is the remover of every dart.
You have pierced through all hardness; I bow down to that Buddha.
You have transcended all fear; you have brought an end to all dread;
you have utterly uprooted all trembling; I bow down to that Buddha.
He who has dried up all greed, who has caused all passion to fade away,
and who has severed all delight— I bow down to that Buddha.
He who has utterly cut off all sorrow and who has neutralized the poison of all hatred.
He has blocked the path to all rebirths; I bow down to that Buddha. 1005.
He has worn away all births; he is extinguished by the fire of all existence;
having transcended the entire world, I bow down to that Buddha. 1006.
I bow down to that Buddha who has desisted from all social intimacy, who shuns all association, and who has relinquished all attachments.
He has completely exhausted all doubts and suppressed all expectations.
He shattered all desires; I bow down to that Buddha. 1008.
He warded off all doubts and severed all afflictions;
he cleansed away all turbidity—I bow down to that Buddha. 1009.
I bow to that Buddha who has utterly uprooted all attachments, who is independent of all abodes, and who has dried up all taints.
He has cast off all acquisitions and has abandoned all objects of sense.
You shattered all conceit—I bow to that Buddha.
You have cast off all distress and abandoned all clinging;
you cut through all covetousness—I bow to that Buddha.
Having severed all fetters, living pure and acting purely;
having transcended attachments and crossed over the flood—to that Buddha I bow. 1013.
He who has stilled all mental distress, by whom all fetters are destroyed;
Freed from all doubt, to that Buddha I bow.
Having transcended all sorrow, dispelling all hindrances,
and liberated from all dejection— to that Buddha I bow.
I bow down to that Buddha who has utterly transcended all fear,
who is entirely devoid of trembling, and who has destroyed all states of agitation.
He who abandoned all possessions and relinquished all attachments.
I bow down to that Buddha who has transcended all desires.
I bow down to that Buddha who possesses the supreme security from bondage, the supreme attainment, and the supreme peace.
I bow down to that Buddha who has completed all that was to be done, who has fulfilled his task, whose faculties are restrained, and who has crossed over the great ocean of delusion.
He has fully understood the mass of suffering and severed the snare of craving.
Completely liberated from all distress, I bow down to that Buddha.
Having transcended all bonds, become cooled, and free from acquisitions;
with the craving for existence utterly exhausted, I bow down to that Buddha.
Having transcended all birth, established in equanimity toward all things, and ever bestowing wise understanding—to that Buddha I bow. 1022.
Detached from becoming, this supreme collection [of aggregates]—
He has abandoned all conditioned phenomena; I bow down to that Buddha.
(1023) Completely liberated from all suffering, the destroyer of hatred and malice, he has torn asunder the fetters of existence; I bow down to that Buddha. (1024)
Wearing a garland of rays, wearing a garland of light, wearing a garland of beams, the drum of Dhamma—you have destroyed the darkness of delusion. To that Buddha, I pay homage.
Like the moon, you bring peace; like the moon, you radiate light.
He established the radiance of peace; I bow to that Buddha.
Like a mass of fire with excellent luster, the heat of his power is an abode of bliss;
illuminated like one who holds a torch, I bow to that Buddha.
Radiant like a mass of light, bestowing illumination upon the entire world—
a most brilliant radiance— to that Buddha I bow. With a splendor exceeding the light of a fathom,
shining with the dawn-red glow of compassion.
Endowed with radiant splendor, I bow down to that Buddha.
Like the moon in the midst of the sky, he shone in the midst of the Saṅgha;
you scattered the light of wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha.
The Kinsman of the Sun, ardent, radiant with a divine form,
who illumines the entire world— to that Buddha I bow.
Amidst the community of ascetics, he shone like the sun.
I bow down to that Buddha, who brings the light of knowledge to the world.
(1032) Like a star among ascetics, possessing a splendor equal to the full moon, the Lord, supreme among all beings—I bow down to that Buddha. (1033)
Bearing the crest of beautiful knowledge, radiant with the splendor of glory, you illuminate the luminous; I bow down to that Buddha. 1034.
Like the maker of day who dispels darkness, blazing and destroying the gloom;
I bow to that Buddha, resplendent with the radiance of six-colored rays.
(1035) Like the moon, stainless and pure, a glorious Supreme Person, perfected with excellent marks—I bow to that Buddha. (1036)
Resplendent like the full moon, with a perfectly tranquil mind, and cooled from every side—I bow down to that Buddha. 1037.
Beautiful to behold, lovely to see, Aṅgīrasa, the Illuminator.
Like the light-maker (the sun) shining forth, I bow to that Buddha. 1038.
Like the moon in the vault of the sky, highly colored and most beautiful, endowed with the great radiance of the Dhamma—I bow to that Buddha. 1039.
Proclaimed and illuminated, shining like the sun;
I bow down to that Buddha of incomparable splendor and radiant power.
The Blessed One has a thousand rays, with a complexion as pure as a lotus.
Surrounded by the radiance of the Dhamma, I bow down to that Buddha.
(1041) Resplendent like a king of sal trees, or like the moon on a full-moon night, he illuminated all directions; I bow down to that Buddha. (1042)
Surrounded by a net of rays, with lotus-face and lotus-eyes, he shines like gold—I bow down to that Buddha. 1043.
Enveloped in the radiance of loving-kindness, illumined as a preacher of the Dhamma;
He caused the radiance of wisdom to blossom; I bow down to that Buddha.
(1044) Like the full moon, he was cleansed and utterly pure;
he purified the True Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha. (1045)
You radiate rays of knowledge, shining brilliantly like the sun of the Dhamma;
you have revealed the path to liberation—I bow down to that Buddha.
Like the full moon in the sky, you bestow cool and radiant light.
I bow down to that Buddha who makes the pure Dhamma shine.
1047. He illuminates the light of the True Dhamma;
radiant and the bearer of radiance, he shines throughout the entire world. I bow down to that Buddha. 1048.
Radiant, the foremost in the three worlds, the excellent illuminator of the True Dhamma,
who has expanded noble knowledge— to that Buddha I pay homage.
Like the moon in the vault of the sky, he is a cool-rayed, brilliant light-maker.
I bow down to that Buddha, the giver of undiminished happiness.
1050. Blazing like a lamp, the dispeller of the darkness of the three worlds, he illuminated the Noble Path; I bow down to that Buddha. 1051.
The maker of light, the bearer of light, the creator of radiance, the possessor of radiance;
the bearer of splendor, the creator of splendor—to that Buddha I bow.
He dispelled the darkness of ignorance, shining with the brilliance of the light of true knowledge.
I bow down to that Buddha who has proclaimed the analysis of the Dhamma. 1053.
