I bow down to that Buddha, the Lord who destroys the darkness of the three worlds, who is radiant with the brilliance of wisdom, and who creates light for the world. 1054.
He dispelled the darkness of delusion, the light-bringer and illuminator;
he proclaimed the Dhamma of Truth—to that Buddha I bow. 1055.
His light is dawned with compassion, revealing the rays of wisdom.
I bow down to that Buddha who has shattered the veil of ignorance.
I bow down to that Buddha who is the source of compassion, nourished by wisdom, who brings light to the three worlds, and who radiates rays of peace.
Like the full moon, beautifully shining, the moon of wisdom, filled with knowledge, he caused the light of the True Dharma to blaze forth—I bow down to that Buddha. 1058.
Having severed the darkness of delusion, Dīpaṅkara shone as a beautiful lamp.
The radiance of enlightenment shone forth; I bow down to that Buddha.
The sun of Dhamma destroyed the darkness of ignorance throughout the three worlds;
you scattered the rays of Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
When the world was shrouded by ignorance, you caused the light of true knowledge to blossom;
you radiated the splendor of the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
You destroyed the night of delusion, a sun made radiant by the Dhamma.
He illuminates both the world and that which lies beyond it; I bow down to that Buddha.
(1062) The sun of the Conqueror, the dispeller of the darkness of the three realms of existence, radiant and full of light; I bow down to that Buddha. (1063)
Bhadda-tejo, Mahā-tejo, Tibba-tejo, Teja-bahu;
Jhāna-tejo, Ñāṇa-tejo—to that Buddha I bow.
Ugga-tejo, Agga-tejo, Puṇṇa-tejo, Tejissara.
The splendor of Brahmā, the splendor of Dharma—bowing my head, I pay homage to that Buddha.
1065. He illuminates all directions, making everything manifest;
great in radiance and exalted—bowing my head, I pay homage to that Buddha. 1066.
To him of vast wisdom, the light-maker, who utterly consumes all darkness, who illuminates the Noble Truths—to that Buddha I bow. 1067.
He who possesses rays, the bearer of rays, who possesses light, the maker of light.
I bow down to that Buddha, the Lord of Light, who possesses a thousand rays.
(1068) I bow down to that Buddha, whose splendor is like the full moon, radiant with the brilliance of wisdom, and who has shattered the darkness of great delusion. (1069)
Seated on the night of the new moon, a great sun of vast radiance, he illuminated the entire world; to that Buddha I bow.
Like a glowing ember, like a lamp of knowledge, he who bears rays of light.
He has dispelled the darkness of delusion; I bow down to that Buddha.
(1071) While all of existence was shrouded in obscurity, he liberated it with the light of knowledge;
he kindled the lamp of the Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha. (1072)
To the destroyer of the darkness of ignorance, the omniscient one, the light from every side, who proclaimed the path of true knowledge—to that Buddha I bow down. 1073.
He who has vanished from everything, yet is in every way the light from every side.
He proclaimed the truth of all truths; I bow down to that Buddha. 1074.
Out of compassion for the entire world, he is the light-maker in the whole world;
removing the darkness from the entire world, I bow down to that Buddha. 1075.
The Seer, seeing all things, proclaimed omniscience and destroyed the root of delusion; I bow down to that Buddha.
Blazing with the power of wisdom, he was a preeminent being of sharp brilliance.
I bow down to that Buddha, who possesses a garland of the light of knowledge and is ardent.
1077. He destroyed the darkness of delusion and was the illuminator of the light of Dhamma;
he proclaimed it to many people—I bow down to that Buddha. 1078.
In a world shrouded by the most terrible darkness, he liberated it with great wisdom;
he proclaimed the light of the Dhamma—to that Buddha, I pay homage.
1079. He shines with the dawn of compassion, dispelling all sorrow.
He has dispelled the darkness of craving; I bow down to that Buddha.
(1080) When the entire world was shrouded in gloom, he became the Lord who brings the light of Dhamma and shatters the blindness of ignorance; I bow down to that Buddha. (1081)
Having severed the veil of ignorance, illuminating the light of true knowledge,
you who create the radiance of the splendor of wisdom— to that Buddha I bow.
You have dispelled the most terrible darkness and shattered the three realms of existence.
He is the sun among men, the supreme sun; I bow down to that Buddha. 1083.
He kindles the light of wisdom, destroying the veil of delusion;
he radiates the splendor of the Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha. 1084.
He illumined the light of the Dhamma, the destroyer of the darkness of evil;
he proclaimed the path to liberation—to that Buddha, I pay homage. 1085.
He kindled the lamp of the Dhamma, the cutter of the veil of evil.
He laid out the path to liberation; I bow down to that Buddha. 1086.
The sun of wisdom, with the radiance of wisdom, he removed the dense darkness of the agitated mind;
he revealed the light of the world; I bow down to that Buddha. 1087.
Blazing with the lamp of the Dhamma, a burner of the darkness of delusion, you illuminate the sublime Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha.
You kindle the light of wisdom, the shatterer of the mass of darkness.
He brought the five aggregates to cessation; I bow down to that Buddha.
The Sun of Dhamma, whose light is capable [of dispelling darkness], has destroyed the darkness of ignorance;
radiant and blazing with light, I bow down to that Buddha.
I bow down to that Buddha, who possesses the treasury of the radiance of wisdom, who illuminates all the world, and who proclaimed the Dhamma of liberation.
He is the destroyer of the darkness of ignorance and the one who makes manifest the light of the Dhamma.
The Illuminator, the Radiant One—I bow down to that Buddha.
(1092) Possessing vitality, perfected in vigor, an ascetic, the crest-jewel of austerity;
adorned with splendor, the Splendid One—I bow down to that Buddha. (1093)
Honored as the auspiciousness of the Dhamma, adorned with the radiance of the Dhamma, well-proclaimed in the Dhamma— to that Buddha I bow.
Adorned with the radiance of wisdom, illuminating the radiance of wisdom.
Possessing the rays of wisdom, possessing the radiance of wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha.
1095. Possessing rays, possessing light, possessing splendor, creating brilliance;
possessing majesty, possessing beauty—I bow down to that Buddha. 1096.
With a radiance equal to ten million suns, as bright as the moon,
sublime and most excellent— homage to that Buddha!
You have stilled all doubts and scattered the army of Māra.
He illuminated the entire world; I bow down to that Buddha.
(1098) Of immeasurable light and incomparable splendor, the giver of immeasurable light in the world;
of immeasurable power and incomparable might—I bow down to that Buddha. (1099)
He illuminated the entire world like the moon freed from clouds;
he shone forth like a blazing fire, like a deity. To that Buddha who elucidated the pure True Dhamma, I pay homage.
1100. Just as a kindled fire, he shone like a divine being.
He shattered great ignorance; I bow down to that Buddha.
(1101) He proclaimed the Dhamma of peace, like the sun dispelling darkness;
he extended peace and tranquility; I bow down to that Buddha. (1102)
Friend of the world, benefactor of the world, kinsman of the world, companion of the world;
you who bring light to the three worlds—to that Buddha I bow. 1103.
You who experience joy and tranquility, and who drink deeply of the flavor of joy in abundance;
Feeding on rapture, with a mind full of joy—I bow down to that Buddha.
Generating rapture and gladness, nourishing the supreme bliss;
devoted to seclusion—I bow down to that Buddha.
The splendor of enlightenment, the radiance of enlightenment, adorned with the halo of enlightenment;
the splendor of the Brahma, the radiance of the Brahma—to that Buddha I bow. 1106.
He whose body is Brahma, whose form is Brahma, who is the Brahmin of Brahma-dhamma.
Brahma’s vessel, become Brahma—I bow down to that Buddha.
Possessing Brahma-like wisdom, a practitioner of the holy life, dwelling in the sublime abodes, knowing the state of Brahma;
possessing the eye of Brahma and the eye of Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
Most helpful and possessed of loving-kindness, with a mind of great compassion, he set forth the method of liberation; I pay homage to that Buddha.
Like a skilled navigator, he carried many across the flood of existence.
I bow down to that Buddha who strove with the impetus of loving-kindness.
I bow down to that Buddha who desires what is wholesome, who is free from craving, who is the abode of infinite compassion, and who knows the incomparable excellence.
Giver of eyes, giver of knowledge, compassionate toward the entire world;
with a mind filled with compassion, I bow down to that Buddha. 1112.
With a virtuous heart, free from cruelty, with a mind of loving-kindness, devoid of anger;
To him whose mind is purified even by abuse—to that Buddha, I pay homage.
(1113) The doer of good, the auspicious one, the leader on the path of goodness, who has reached the perfection of goodness—to that Buddha, I pay homage. (1114)
I bow down to that Buddha who acts with boundless compassion, who is a vast treasury of abundant compassion, and who is the profound abode of compassion.
He is the Greatly Compassionate One, the steadfast hero, an ocean of compassion and wisdom.
To him who acts with exceeding compassion, that Buddha, I bow down.
He who performs what is wholesome, compassionate, a friend of virtue,
and full of loving-kindness— teaching the sublime Dhamma, to that Buddha I bow down.
The Protector whose heart is filled with compassion,
who is secure and whose mind is intent on security, who is joyful and gladdening— I bow down to that Buddha.
Having renounced the status of a wheel-turning monarch, the Awakened One attained omniscience.
I bow down to that Buddha, the ocean of compassion without remainder.
(1119) He who extinguished the great fire of anger and hatred with the water of loving-kindness;
I bow down to that Buddha, the benefactor of the entire world. (1120)
With a mind cooled by compassion, compassionate toward all beings, and endowed with virtuous qualities—I bow down to that Buddha. 1121.
An ocean of mercy, a treasury of pity, merciful, and a sea of compassion;
The Lord of Compassion, the Protector of Compassion—to that Buddha I bow.
He who is of great compassion, of great exaltation, of great abiding, the Great Sage;
ever compassionate, ever-abiding—to that Buddha I bow.
The giver of benefit to all beings, the giver of happiness to all,
the bringer of peace to all living creatures— to that Buddha I bow down.
Like Pajjunna raining upon all creatures with a cloud of Dhamma, he has showered it forth.
I bow down to that Buddha who brings peace and happiness to the world.
1125. I bow down to that Buddha, the seer who looks upon others, serves others, brings happiness to others, seeks the welfare of others, and desires the benefit of others. 1126.
He proclaimed the Four Noble Truths out of compassion for living beings;
he delivered many people across [the flood]. To that Buddha, I pay homage. 1127.
Ever holy, he was a giver of peace; ever happy, he was a giver of happiness.
He rained down the cloud of Dhamma; I bow to that Buddha.
(1128) For the welfare and benefit of many people, he wandered through many existences; he uplifted many people; I bow to that Buddha. (1129)
For the welfare and happiness of many, you fulfilled the perfections;
you sought the path to liberation—I bow down to that Buddha. 1130.
With a mind perfected in all respects, compassionate toward all living beings;
At all times with a compassionate heart, I bow down to that Buddha. 1131.
Friend to all, companion to all, compassionate toward all beings, and the benefactor of all creatures—I bow down to that Buddha. 1132.
Thinking of the welfare of all, bringing happiness to all, compassionate toward all—to that Buddha I bow. 1133.
With limbs perfectly delicate, beautiful in every major and minor limb;
Worthy of praise and worthy of homage, I bow down to that Buddha.
Adorned with every beauty, graced with every majesty,
beloved by all beings, I bow down to that Buddha.
Radiant, most pleasing, handsome, and possessed of beautiful form;
with peerless complexion and golden hue—to that Buddha I bow. 1136.
Of lovely complexion and lovely form, of lovely fame and lovely renown.
He whose splendor is lovely and whose radiance is lovely—I bow down to that Buddha.
(1137) The wise one who has attained the six supernormal powers, whose complexion is radiant and beautiful, and who shines with six-colored rays—I bow down to that Buddha. (1138)
Resembling a priceless golden ornament, faultless with skin like refined gold, with a face as radiant as gold—I bow down to that Buddha. 1139.
With his splendors he illumines all, revealing the path to liberation.
Surrounded by rays of Dhamma, I bow down to that Buddha.
(1140) With a jaw like a lion’s and shoulders like an elephant’s, adorned with the luster of wisdom, he is fair-faced and beautiful; I bow down to that Buddha. (1141)
Endowed with beauty, giver of beauty, captivating, delighter of the mind;
he gladdened all people—to that Buddha I bow. 1142.
Golden, golden-hued, the color of gold, supreme in color;
Golden-hued, with golden hair—him, the Buddha, I bow down to. 1143.
With a lovely body, lovely splendor, lovely radiance, and lovely luster;
lovely to behold and full of loveliness—him, the Buddha, I bow down to. 1144.
With soft, white, and prominent lips, and a row of teeth without gaps;
with high-arched feet—O Blessed One, I bow down to that Buddha.
With a long body, a long tongue, long arms, and long fingers;
With hands and feet very firm, I bow down to that Buddha.
(1146) With a Brahma-like voice, antelope-like calves, and an upright body, equal to Brahmā;
knowing flavors, the supreme among those who perceive flavors—I bow down to that Buddha. (1147)
With blue eyes and long heels, with a high nose like refined gold,
and feet marked by the excellent wheel— to that Buddha I bow.
With forty even teeth, and eyelashes like those of a young calf.
With the upper half of his body like that of a lion, to that Buddha I bow.
(1149) With a single hair growing from each pore and skin like gold, endowed with white tusks, to that Buddha I bow. (1150)
With deep blue hair on the upper body, adorned with a golden-hued fathom-wide aura,
and webbed hands and feet— I bow down to that Buddha.
With the private parts concealed in a sheath, he has well-placed feet.
I bow down to that Buddha whose head is adorned with the crest-jewel of Siṃhahanu.
1152. I bow down to that Buddha who possesses all the marks of a Great Man, who bears the thirty-two primary characteristics, and who has the eighty secondary marks. 1153.
Exceedingly charming, exceedingly delightful, and exceedingly captivating—I bow down to that Buddha. 1154.
He is supremely lovely, beloved, beautiful, and pleasing to behold.
Endowed with the thirty-two marks, I bow down to that Buddha.
Radiant as a lover, golden-hued, with a face and eyes like gold,
resembling the mountain of gold— I bow down to that Buddha.
Desirable and lovely, radiating splendor like gold;
possessing form with eyes like lotus petals—to that Buddha I bow. 1157.
Of auspicious appearance and brilliant, like the shining mountain of gold.
Possessing power and divine vision, I bow down to that Buddha.
(1158) Adorned with excellent marks, beautiful in every way and in all respects;
gentle and radiant in every limb, I bow down to that Buddha. (1159)
A mine of virtues, worthy of honor, with a voice like the song of the *karavīka* bird, adorned with the most excellent marks—I bow to that Buddha. 1160.
Great-bodied, of sublime body, a body like Brahmā’s, with a body upright.
With a body that is both radiant and serene, I bow down to that Buddha.
With limbs of ultimate delicacy, with skin of ultimate softness and fineness,
and with a countenance of ultimate beauty— O Lord, I bow down to that Buddha.
Jananetta, Janamoḷi, with eyes and face full of serene confidence, and with eyes like white water-lilies—to that Buddha I bow down. 1163.
With a serene mind and clear faith, most excellent and exceedingly beautiful.
Utterly pure and supreme—I bow down to that Buddha.
(1164) Of auspicious form, of blessed form, speaking auspiciously, with an auspicious face;
radiant and exceedingly brilliant—I bow down to that Buddha. (1165)
Mañjughosa, Mañjuvāṇī, Mañjubhāṇī, Mañjussara;
Mañjubhāsī, Mudubhāsī—to that Buddha I bow down. 1166.
Mudukāya, Muducitta, Muduka, Mudulakkhaṇa;
Gentle-minded and gentle-spoken, I bow down to that Buddha.
Endowed with excellent marks and possessed of all limbs,
supreme in the entire world, I bow down to that Buddha.
Susobhita, endowed with splendor, adorned with the ornament of peace—
I bow down to that Buddha, the lofty banner of the three worlds.
Having crossed the terrible flood of saṃsāra, he is adorned with the ornaments of liberation.
I bow down to that Buddha, who is well-yoked with wisdom and endowed with excellent virtues.
1170. I bow down to that Buddha, who is perfectly endowed with all virtues, adorned with the ornament of moral conduct, and the most supreme jewel of the True Dharma. 1171.
I bow down to that Buddha, whose fame and praise are infinite, who is honored by all in saṃsāra, renowned, celebrated, and worthy of worship. 1172.
He is well-honored throughout the entire world and esteemed by all the world.
Honored by the entire world, I bow down to that Buddha. 1173.
Worshipped by the God of Gods, the Great God, and the Guide;
renowned as the Beloved of the Three Realms, I bow down to that Buddha. 1174.
Worthy of being seen, worthy of praise, worthy of commendation, the foremost;
worthy of description, worthy of homage—to that Buddha I bow down. 1175.
Inspiring confidence, he is confident; gracious, he is tranquil.
Worthy of worship, worthy of veneration—I bow down to that Buddha.
Honored, revered, renowned, and saluted;
having attained blameless and pure virtue—I bow down to that Buddha.
Honored even more by the world of beings, having gone from this shore to the further shore, faultless and crowned with wisdom—to that Buddha I bow down. 1178.
Powerful and fruitful, he is highly esteemed by many.
Of great benefit to the world, to that Buddha I bow.
Worshipped by the entire world, honored by the entire world;
revered by humans and gods, to that Buddha I bow.
Supreme among the worlds, worthy of worship, highly honored and revered;
cherished, beloved, and sustained by praise and renown—to that Buddha I bow.
1181. Renowned, widely celebrated, excellently famed, universally acclaimed, and venerated.
I bow down to that Buddha who is superior in beauty, who is expansive.
I bow down to that Buddha who is the most excellent of all, the eldest of all, the purest of all, the highest of all; who is honored and revered by all.
He who brought all the gods under his influence, the guide of all the gods, the Lord honored by the three worlds—to that Buddha I bow. 1184.
He who is the leader of the entire world, the healer of the entire world.
The best of all, established in the Dhamma— to that Buddha I bow.
The Hero who has overcome the entire world, the Victor supreme over the entire world,
renowned throughout the whole world— to that Buddha I bow.
Perfect in all higher knowledges, renowned throughout the entire world, the one with all-seeing eyes, the accomplished one—I bow down to that Buddha. 1187.
The Protector who benefits the whole world, the bringer of happiness to the whole world.
Worshipped by the entire world, I bow down to that Buddha.
Desiring nothing at all, with every craving cut off in every way,
having crossed the ocean of great thirst— I bow down to that Buddha.
Just as he saw it, so he declared it; in every way his mind was fixed on truth.
He made known that which is not otherwise—homage to you, the Buddha! 1190.
Knower of knowledge, perfected in knowledge, perfected in wisdom, possessed of wisdom.
Victorious in the Dhamma, peaceful in the Dhamma—I bow down to that Buddha.
(1191) Perfectly endowed with excellent virtues, a good man, a virtuous person, and one of noble intellect;
an ocean of great wisdom—I bow down to that Buddha. (1192)
To him who sees names, who sees forms, the ascetic and treasury of austerity, who possesses insight into things as they truly are—to that Buddha I bow. 1193.
The Leader is endowed with the eighteen qualities of a Buddha.
Having attained the bases of psychic power, the great adept—I bow down to that Buddha. 1194.
Having attained virtue and concentration, having attained the wisdom that leads to liberation;
having attained the perfection of all qualities—I bow down to that Buddha. 1195.

I bow down to that Buddha who has attained the perfectly pure Dhamma, who dispels all perversions, and who has crossed over the ocean of the three realms of existence. He extinguished the fire of passion,
became cooled himself, and is the maker of coolness for others.
He caused the rain of the nectar of peace to fall; I bow down to that Buddha.
Having thoroughly crushed the sectarians and having set aside false conceits, he established them in the true Dhamma; I bow down to that Buddha.
Liberated from attachment to the human realm, you have transcended attachment to the divine;
freed from all attachments, I bow down to that Buddha. 1199. You are the remover of the darkness of the three realms of existence, the bearer of the radiance of the knowledge of enlightenment.
The illuminator of the Dhamma, worthy of honor—I bow down to that Buddha.
One possessed of jhāna, perfected in jhāna, the destroyer of the realm of ignorance;
well-jhāned, a master of great jhāna—I bow down to that Buddha.
The Naga who has attained the destruction of craving,
who severs the conduit to existence, and who has crushed all attachment— to that Buddha I bow down.
He has carried away all karmic defilements without exception.
The River of Dhamma has flowed forth; I bow down to that Buddha. 1203.
He who has attained self-control, attained the Yamā, attained the Samā, and whose conduct is harmonious;
he who has reached the state that is firm and eternal—I bow down to that Buddha. 1204.
Wise, possessed of understanding, intelligent, and a treasury of wisdom;
endowed with insight and a mind of loving-kindness—to that Buddha I bow.
Skilled in what is possible and impossible, and exceedingly proficient in all phenomena.
Having attained wisdom and being possessed of great intelligence, I bow down to that Buddha. 1206.

Having crossed over the flood of the suffering of existence, having reached the further shore through the abandonment of craving, and having destroyed the darkness of ignorance, I bow down to that Buddha. 1207.
Steadfast-hearted and courageous, restrained and self-controlled in mind, with guarded senses and guarded thoughts—I bow down to that Buddha. 1208.
Well-restrained, with peaceful senses, contented and well-composed.
Perfect in true knowledge and conduct, I bow down to that Buddha. 1209.
You have crushed the wheel of birth; now there is no further becoming.
Having crossed over the flood of the three worlds, I bow down to that Buddha. 1210.
Unassociated with both householders and those without homes,
wandering without a fixed abode and free from attachment— to that Buddha I bow.
Having abandoned birth and death, unclinging, he has attained Nibbāna.
He has crossed the ocean of saṃsāra; I bow down to that Buddha.
Seeking the path, the knower of the path, the proclaimer of the path, the Tathāgata who has seen the path to the Deathless; I bow down to that Buddha.
Just as he saw and proclaimed it, so do I bow down to that Buddha—the Blessed One of vast wisdom, the Lord free from desire and stainless. 1214.
The Lord of Sages, supreme among the silent ones, has transcended both delight and aversion.
Transcending fear, transcending existence— to that Buddha I bow.
The awakened leader, the exceedingly great benefactor,
the giver of all supreme happiness— to that Buddha I bow.
Stainless and free from stain, immaculate, having cleansed away impurity;
crushing pride and devoid of arrogance—to that Buddha I bow down.
Honored, revered, praised, and saluted.
Worshipped by gods and humans, I bow down to that Buddha.
(1218) Adorned with the radiance of fathom-wide light, bearing the thirty-two marks, and perfected with the secondary characteristics, I bow down to that Buddha. (1219)
Without rod or weapon, you governed by the Dhamma;
you uplifted many beings—to that Buddha I bow down. 1220.
Blessed one, you who drink the nectar of the Dhamma, you who destroy the poison of craving.
You have ground away all ignorance; I bow down to that Buddha.
(1221) Fortunate is the Protector! Fortunate is the Master! Fortunate is the Sage who has overcome Māra!
Fortunate is the victor in battle! I bow down to that Buddha. (1222)
Delighting in jhāna, rejoicing in jhāna; delighting in the Dhamma, rejoicing in the Dhamma—O, how wonderful!
O, how wonderful! You have gone to the further shore; I bow down to that Buddha.
Like a white lotus, unstained—behold his purity!
To that one whose mind is unshakable, I bow down to that Buddha.
1224. Oh, Buddha! Oh, Pure One! Oh, You of perfectly purified mind!
Oh, oh, Ocean of Loving-kindness! To that Buddha, I bow down. 1225.
Homage, homage to you who are pure in virtue, pure in mind, and pure in view!
Homage, homage to you who dwell in the Dhamma, who bring auspiciousness, and who work for the welfare of people!
Homage, homage to you who are a great ascetic, who possess insight into the Dhamma, and who see the inexhaustible!
Seeker of the path, seeker of the world’s welfare, Great Seer of the Buddha—homage, homage!
